nahhas-irab:40-40.t: (وَقَدْ بَلَغَنِيَ الْكِبَرُ): «بلغني الكبر» and «بلغت الكبر» are one and the same. (وَامْرَأَتِي عاقِرٌ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). «عاقر» is without hāʾ (the feminine tāʾ) because it is a relational form (ʿalā al-nasab); had it been formed on the verb, one would have said: «عقرت فهي عقيرة», as though she had a barrenness (ʿuqr) that prevented her from giving birth. (قالَ كَذلِكَ اللَّهُ يَفْعَلُ ما يَشاءُ): the kāf is in the position of the accusative, i.e. He does what He wills like that.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t:
(قالَ رَبِّ اجْعَلْ لِي آيَةً): (اجْعَلْ) means «صيّر» (make into), and for that reason it must take two objects, and «لي» is in the position of the second. When it means «خلق» (create), it takes only one object, as in His saying: خَلَقَ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهارَ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 33]. (قالَ آيَتُكَ): mubtadaʾ (subject). (أَلَّا تُكَلِّمَ النَّاسَ): its khabar (predicate). The nominative of «تكلّم» is also permissible, in the sense «أنك لا تكلّم الناس» (that you will not speak to people), like أَلَّا يَرْجِعُ إِلَيْهِمْ قَوْلًا [Ṭā Hā: 89]; the Kufans say the nominative is on the basis that «لا» has the meaning of «ليس». (ثَلاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ): an adverbial (ẓarf). We have already mentioned the view of Qatāda that Zakariyyāʾ was punished with being prevented from speech when he asked; this is a view to be shunned, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not tell us that Zakariyyāʾ committed a sin, nor that He had forbidden him from this. The correct view on it is that the meaning is: make for me a sign that indicates the coming into being of the child, since that was hidden from me. Al-Akhfash said: (إِلَّا رَمْزاً) is an exception not of the same kind as the first (istithnāʾ laysa min al-awwal). Al-Kisāʾī said: one says «رمز يرمز» and «يرمز». ʿAlqama ibn Qays read إِلَّا رَمْزاً and al-Aʿmash read إِلَّا رَمْزاً [Translator's note: the two variant vowellings (presumably رَمَزًا and رُمُزًا) are not distinguished in the printed text], and these two are nouns, while the form with the sukūn is the maṣdar (verbal noun).
(وَسَبِّحْ): an imperative, i.e. declare Allah, Majestic and Mighty, free of what the polytheists say. It has also been said: «سبّح» means pray, and from this comes «فرغ فلان من سبحته» (so-and-so finished his supererogatory prayer). (بِالْعَشِيِّ): it has been said that it is a plural, and it has been said that it is a singular; the better view is that it is a singular, for the future. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: one says «أنا آتيك عشيّ غد» (I will come to you tomorrow evening), «أنا آتيك عشيّة اليوم» (I will come to you this evening), «أتيته عشيّة أمس» and «عشيّ أمس» (I came to him yesterday evening).

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: (إِنَّ اللَّهَ اصْطَفاكِ): the ṭāʾ is substituted for a tāʾ, because the ṭāʾ is more similar to the ṣād.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t: (يا مَرْيَمُ اقْنُتِي): an imperative, and for that reason the nūn has been dropped from it. (وَاسْجُدِي): conjoined to it. One says «سجد» when someone lowers himself and is humbled, and «ركع» when he bends over; from this one says: «ركع الشيخ» (the old man became bent). (مع الراكعين) may mean: bow with those who pray in congregation, and it may mean: be among those who bow, even if you do not pray with them.

nahhas-irab:44-44.t: (ذلِكَ) is in the position of the nominative, i.e. «الأمر ذلك» (the matter is that), so it is the khabar (predicate) of «الأمر»; it may also be in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar being (مِنْ أَنْباءِ الْغَيْبِ). (وَما كُنْتَ لَدَيْهِمْ إِذْ يُلْقُونَ أَقْلامَهُمْ): «إذ» is in the position of the accusative, i.e. you were not with them at that time. (أَقْلامَهُمْ) is the plural of «قلم», from «قلمه» when one cuts it. We have mentioned that it has been said that «أقلامهم» are their arrows (for casting lots); better than this view is: their pens with which they used to write the revelation; they gathered them and threw them into a river to see which of them would go against the current of the water, so that its owner would be the one to take charge of Maryam (يكفل مريم), i.e. guarantee to look after her affairs. As for the pens being divining arrows (al-qidāḥ), that is far-fetched, because these are the azlām which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forbade; however, it is possible that they did that in a manner other than the way the people of the Jāhiliyya used to do it. (أَيُّهُمْ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and it is attached to an omitted verb, i.e. they look to see which of them would take charge of Maryam. Sībawayh related: «اذهب فانظر زيد أبو من هو؟» (go and see Zayd — whose father is he?); if you put it in the accusative, the meaning is reversed.

nahhas-irab:45-45.t: (إِذْ قالَتِ الْمَلائِكَةُ) is attached to «يختصمون», and it may be attached to His saying «وما كنت لديهم». (بِكَلِمَةٍ مِنْهُ اسْمُهُ الْمَسِيحُ): He did not say «اسمها» (its name, feminine) because the meaning of «كلمة» (word) is a child. Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī said: «المسيح» is «الصدّيق» (the truthful one). Abū ʿUbayd said: in their language it is «مسيحا». It has also been said that he was called al-Masīḥ only because he was anointed (musiḥa) with an oil of fragrant scent with which the prophets used to be anointed, so that when someone was anointed with it, it was known that he was a prophet. «عيسى» is a non-Arabic (aʿjamī) name, and for that reason it is a diptote; and if you take it as Arabic, it is a diptote both when definite and indefinite, because it contains the alif of femininity, and it would be derived from «عاسه يعوسه» when one manages him and takes care of him; it may also be derived from «العيس» and from «العيس» [Translator's note: the two words are printed identically; presumably «العَيْس» (camel's semen) and «العِيس» (whitish camels) are meant]. Al-Akhfash said: (وَجِيهاً) is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Al-Farrāʾ said: it is accusative by «al-qaṭʿ» (severance). Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: the accusative by «al-qaṭʿ» is an absurd expression, because the meaning is that he was given the glad tidings of ʿĪsā in this state; and he did not explain the meaning of al-qaṭʿ. If al-qaṭʿ is a semantic notion, he did not explain what it is; if it is a formal (verbal) factor, he did not explain what the governing factor (al-ʿāmil) is; and if he means that the alif and lām were severed from it, this is absurd, because the ḥāl can only be indefinite, and the alif and lām are for something already known — so how can something be severed from it that was never in it at all? Al-Akhfash said: (وَمِنَ الْمُقَرَّبِينَ) is conjoined to «وجيه», i.e. «ومقرّبا» (and brought near). The plural of «وجيه» is «وجهاء» and «وجاه».

nahhas-irab:46-46.t:
Al-Akhfash said: (وَيُكَلِّمُ) is conjoined to «وجيها». Al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ said: (وَكَهْلًا) is conjoined to «وجيها».
Abū Isḥāq said: «وكهلا» means «ويكلّم الناس كهلا» (and he will speak to people as a man of middle age). Ibn Jurayj related from Mujāhid, who said: «الكهل» is the forbearing one. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is not known in the language; «الكهل» according to the lexicographers is one who has approached forty. Some of them said: he is called «حدث» (a youth) up to sixteen years, then «شابّ» (a young man) up to thirty-two years, then he becomes «يكتهل» (a man of middle age) at thirty-three. Al-Akhfash said: (وَمِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ) is conjoined to «وجيها».

nahhas-irab:47-47.t: (إِذا قَضى أَمْراً فَإِنَّما يَقُولُ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ): conjoined to «يقول», and it may be cut off (from what precedes), i.e. «فهو يكون» (and so it is). The scholars have spoken about its meaning. It has been said: it is treated as something existent that is addressed, because what He, Majestic and Mighty, wills must necessarily come to be, so on this basis it was addressed. It has been said: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, informed us of the speed of what He wills, that it is like this. It has been said: it is His sign for what He wills, just as ʿĪsā's (peace be upon him) breathing into the bird was a sign of Allah's, Majestic and Mighty, creating it. It has been said: i.e. He brings it out of non-existence into existence, so the servants were addressed in terms of what they know. And it has been said: «له» means «من أجله» (for its sake), as you say «أنا أكرم فلانا لك» (I honour so-and-so for you), i.e. for your sake.

nahhas-irab:48-48.t: (وَيُعَلِّمُهُ الْكِتابَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ): Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read «ونعلّمه» with nūn, referring it back to His saying نُوحِيهِ [Āl ʿImrān: 44]. The yāʾ is preferable, because of His saying وَإِذا قَضى أَمْراً فَإِنَّما يَقُولُ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ, so the yāʾ is nearer. Al-Akhfash said: (وَيُعَلِّمُهُ) is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to «وجيها».

nahhas-irab:49-49.t:
(وَرَسُولًا إِلى بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ): there are two views on its accusative. One of them is that the implied construction is «ويجعله رسولا» (and He will make him a messenger), and the other is «ويكلّمهم رسولا» (and he will speak to them as a messenger). (أَنِّي قَدْ جِئْتُكُمْ), i.e. «بأني», so «أنّ» is in the position of the accusative. (أَنِّي أَخْلُقُ لَكُمْ مِنَ الطِّينِ كَهَيْئَةِ الطَّيْرِ) is a badal (substitute) from it; it may be in the position of the genitive as a badal from «آية»; and it may be in the position of the nominative with an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. «هي أنّي أخلق لكم من الطين كهيئة الطير» (it is that I create for you from clay the like of the form of a bird). (فَأَنْفُخُ فِيهِ فَيَكُونُ طَيْراً بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ): this is the reading of Abū ʿAmr and the people of Kufa. Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ read «كهيئة الطّائر فأنفخ فيه فيكون طائرا», and Nāfiʿ read «كهيئة الطير فأنفخ فيه فيكون طائرا». The first two readings are clearer. The implied construction in this one is: then I breathe into the single one of them, or of it, because «الطير» is treated as both masculine and feminine; so the single one is «طائر», and «طائر» and «طير» are like «تاجر» (merchant) and «تجر» (merchants).
(وَأُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِما تَأْكُلُونَ), i.e. of that which you eat; and «ما» together with the verb may be a maṣdar (verbal noun). (وَما تَدَّخِرُونَ): Mujāhid, al-Zuhrī and Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī read «وما تذخرون» with a dotted dhāl, unstressed. Al-Farrāʾ said: its origin is the dhāl, meaning «تذخرون» from «ذخرت»; the origin is «تذتخرون», and combining the dhāl and the tāʾ was heavy on the tongue, so they assimilated; but they disliked that the tāʾ should disappear into the dhāl, so that the meaning of the iftiʿāl form would be lost, so they brought a letter intermediate between the two, which is the dāl, and said «تدّخرون». Abū Jaʿfar said: this view is a clear error, because if they had assimilated as he said, they would have had to assimilate the dhāl into the tāʾ, since the rule in assimilation is that the first is assimilated into the second; so how would the tāʾ disappear? The correct view on this is the doctrine of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh: the dhāl is a voiced (majhūr) letter that prevents the breath from flowing, and the tāʾ is a voiceless (mahmūs) letter with which the breath flows, so they substituted, from the place of articulation of the tāʾ, a voiced letter resembling the dhāl in its voicing, giving «تذدخرون»; then the dhāl was assimilated into the dāl, giving «تدّخرون». Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh said: if you wish, you may assimilate the dāl into the dhāl and say «تذّخرون», but this is not the preferred way.

nahhas-irab:50-50.t:
(وَمُصَدِّقاً لِما بَيْنَ يَدَيَّ مِنَ التَّوْراةِ), i.e. «وجئتكم مصدّقا» (and I have come to you confirming). Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā [Thaʿlab] said: it cannot be conjoined to «وجيها», because if it were so, it would have had to be «لما بين يديه» (what is before him).
(وَلِأُحِلَّ لَكُمْ): there is an ellipsis here, so that the lām of kay (purpose) has something to be attached to, i.e. «ولأحلّ لكم جئتكم» (and I have come to you to make lawful for you). We have already mentioned its meaning, and we add further explanation: it has been said that ʿĪsā (peace be upon him) made lawful for them only what had been forbidden to them on account of their sins and was not in the Torah, such as eating fats and every animal with claws. It has also been said: ʿĪsā (peace be upon him) made lawful for them things which the rabbis had forbidden them, which had not been forbidden to them in the Torah.

nahhas-irab:51-51.t: (إِنَّ اللَّهَ رَبِّي وَرَبُّكُمْ): with kasra on «إن», as a new start (ʿalā al-ibtidāʾ). Abū Ḥātim related from al-Akhfash «أنّ» with fatḥa, as a badal (substitute) from «آية»; Abū Ḥātim rejected it and claimed that it has no justification. He said: because the sign (al-āya) is the token which they had not seen, so how could it be a statement? Abū Jaʿfar said: this is not how those who transmit accurately reported it from al-Akhfash, nor is it so in his books; the sound report from him is that he said: some related «أنّ الله» with fatḥa on «أن», in the sense «وجئتكم بأن الله ربّي وربّكم» (and I have come to you with [the message] that Allah is my Lord and your Lord), and this is a good view.

nahhas-irab:52-52.t: (فَلَمَّا أَحَسَّ عِيسى مِنْهُمُ الْكُفْرَ): al-Farrāʾ said: they intended to kill him. Abū Jaʿfar said: one says «أحسست» and «أحست», like «ظللت» and «ظلت», and «حسيت» is also related in the sense of «علمت» and «عرفت» (I knew, I perceived). (قالَ مَنْ أَنْصارِي إِلَى اللَّهِ): al-Akhfash said: the singular of «الأنصار» is «نصير», like «شريف» and «أشراف», and «ناصر», like «صاحب» and «أصحاب». Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: the Arabs say «نصر» for the singular of «الأنصار»; they likened faʿl to faʿal. (وَاشْهَدْ بِأَنَّا): the origin is «بأننا»; the nūn was dropped for lightness, and likewise إِنِّي مُتَوَفِّيكَ [Āl ʿImrān: 55]. The one who plots (al-mākir) is the one who uses a ruse against the one he is scheming against; and plotting (al-makr) from Allah, Majestic and Mighty, is requital and justice; on this basis is وَاللَّهُ خَيْرُ الْماكِرِينَ [Āl ʿImrān: 54].

nahhas-irab:55-55.t: (إِنِّي مُتَوَفِّيكَ): the origin is «متوفّيُك»; the ḍamma was dropped because of its heaviness, and it is the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ». (وَرافِعُكَ) is conjoined to it, and likewise (وَمُطَهِّرُكَ), and likewise (وَجاعِلُ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوكَ); «وجاعلٌ الذين اتبعوك» is also permissible, and that is the original form. It has been said that the complete stop (al-tamām) is at His saying «ومطهّرك من الذين كفروا», and this is a good view, indicated by the ḥadīth and by reasoning. As for the ḥadīth: Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Firyābī narrated to us: Ibrāhīm ibn al-ʿAlāʾ al-Zubaydī narrated to us: al-Walīd ibn Muslim narrated to us: Marwān ibn Janāḥ narrated to us, from Yūnus ibn Maysara ibn Ḥalbas, from Muʿāwiya ibn Abī Sufyān, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us while we were in the mosque talking, and he said: «Are you saying that I am the last of you to die? We said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said: I am the first of you to die», and he mentioned the ḥadīth, and at its end he said: and he recited إِذْ قالَ اللَّهُ يا عِيسى إِنِّي مُتَوَفِّيكَ وَرافِعُكَ إِلَيَّ وَمُطَهِّرُكَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَجاعِلُ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوكَ «O Muḥammad» فَوْقَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِلى يَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ. Abū Jaʿfar said: as for reasoning, the Qur'an was sent down upon the Prophet ﷺ, so every address in it is to him unless some indication occurs [to the contrary]; on this basis His saying, Majestic and Mighty, وَأَذِّنْ فِي النَّاسِ بِالْحَجِّ [al-Ḥajj: 27] must be addressed to the Prophet ﷺ.

nahhas-irab:56-57.t: (فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is (فَأُعَذِّبُهُمْ); «الذين» may also be in the position of the accusative with an implied verb, and likewise (وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ فَيُوَفِّيهِمْ أُجُورَهُمْ). Sībawayh related وَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَهَدَيْناهُمْ [Fuṣṣilat: 17] in the accusative. Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Khālid narrated to us: Khalaf ibn Hishām narrated to us: al-Khaffāf narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl, from al-Ḥasan, that he read «وأما الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصّالحات فنوفّيهم أجورهم» (with nūn). Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning is the same, i.e. Allah will pay them their wages in full.

nahhas-irab:58-58.t: (ذلِكَ نَتْلُوهُ عَلَيْكَ): (ذلِكَ) is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is (نَتْلُوهُ). It may be in the position of the nominative with an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. «الأمر ذلك» (the matter is that), and it may be in the position of the accusative with an implied verb. Abū Isḥāq said: «ذلك» may have the meaning of «الذي» (which), with «نتلوه» as its ṣila (relative clause), and the khabar is (مِنَ الْآياتِ).

nahhas-irab:59-59.t: (كَمَثَلِ آدَمَ): the statement is complete here; then He said (خَلَقَهُ مِنْ تُرابٍ ثُمَّ قالَ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ), i.e. «فكان» (and he was); the imperfect stands in the place of the past when the meaning is known.

nahhas-irab:60-60.t: Al-Farrāʾ said: (الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّكَ) is nominative with an implied «هو» (it is).

nahhas-irab:61-61.t:
(فَمَنْ حَاجَّكَ فِيهِ): a condition, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is the fāʾ and what follows it. Ibn ʿAbbās said: they are the people of Najrān: al-Sayyid, al-ʿĀqib and Abū al-Ḥārith. (تَعالَوْا): an imperative in which there is the sense of urging and of making the proof clear.
(نَدْعُ): the answer to the imperative, jussive (majzūm). (ثُمَّ نَبْتَهِلْ): conjoined to it. Abū ʿUbayda related «بهله الله يبهله بهلة», i.e. He cursed him; and «نبتهل» means we pray for the curse. (فَنَجْعَلْ لَعْنَتَ اللَّهِ عَلَى الْكاذِبِينَ): conjoined.

nahhas-irab:62-62.t: (إِنَّ هذا لَهُوَ الْقَصَصُ الْحَقُّ): «هو» is redundant (zāʾida), a separating pronoun (fāṣila) according to the Basrans; it may also be a mubtadaʾ (subject), with (الْقَصَصُ) as its khabar (predicate) and the clause the khabar of «إنّ». (وَما مِنْ إِلهٍ إِلَّا اللَّهُ): the accusative [«إلا اللهَ»] is also permissible, as an exception.

nahhas-irab:63-63.t: (فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ بِالْمُفْسِدِينَ): a protasis and its apodosis. «تولّوا» is a past verb in which the jussive does not appear; it may also be an imperfect, the origin being «تتولّوا».

nahhas-irab:64-64.t: (قُلْ يا أَهْلَ الْكِتابِ تَعالَوْا إِلى كَلِمَةٍ): Qaʿnab read «كِلْمة»; he threw the vowel of the lām onto the kāf, as one says «كِبْد». Abū al-ʿĀliya said: the word (al-kalima) is «لا إله إلّا الله». (سَواءٍ) is a naʿt (adjective) of «كلمة»; al-Ḥasan read «سواءً» in the accusative, i.e. «استوت استواء» (it is equitable, an equity). Qatāda said: «السواء» is justice. Al-Farrāʾ said: in the sense of justice one also says «سِوى» and «سُوى». He said: and in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] it is «إلى كلمة عدل بيننا وبينكم». (أَلَّا نَعْبُدَ إِلَّا اللَّهَ): as a badal (substitute) from «كلمة»; or, if you wish, the implied construction is «هي أن لا نعبد إلّا الله» (it is that we worship none but Allah). (وَلا نُشْرِكَ بِهِ شَيْئاً): al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ said: it is also permissible to say وَلا نُشْرِكَ بِهِ شَيْئاً وَلا يَتَّخِذَ بَعْضُنا بَعْضاً in the jussive, by «tawahhum» (imagining) that there is no «أن» at the beginning of the statement. Abū Jaʿfar said: nothing is achieved by «tawahhum»; rather, the doctrine of Sībawayh is that «نعبد» and what follows it may be jussive on the basis that «أن» is explicative (mufassira), in the sense of «أي», as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: أَنِ امْشُوا [Ṣād: 6], with «لا» being the jussive-governing lā. On this basis «نعبد» and what follows may also be nominative, as a statement; and the nominative is also permissible in the sense «أنّه لا نعبد» (that we do not worship), and like it is أَلَّا يَرْجِعُ إِلَيْهِمْ قَوْلًا [Ṭā Hā: 89]. The meaning of وَلا يَتَّخِذَ بَعْضُنا بَعْضاً أَرْباباً مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ is: we do not worship ʿĪsā, because he is a human being like us, and we do not accept from the monks their forbidding us what Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has not forbidden us, for then we would have taken them as lords.

nahhas-irab:65-65.t: (يا أَهْلَ الْكِتابِ لِمَ تُحَاجُّونَ فِي إِبْراهِيمَ): the origin is «لما»; the alif was dropped because the preposition is a compensation for it, and to distinguish between the interrogative and the statement (khabar). The dropping was not permitted in the statement because there the alif is medial.

nahhas-irab:66-66.t:
(ها أَنْتُمْ هؤُلاءِ حاجَجْتُمْ): Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said: the origin is «أأنتم»; the first hamza was replaced by a hāʾ because it is its sister. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a good view; al-Farrāʾ has a doctrine about this noun when the hāʾ is prefixed to it, and we will mention it later. Al-Ḥasan and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf the Jew and his companions, and a group of the Christians, said: Ibrāhīm is one of us. So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, revealed ما كانَ إِبْراهِيمُ يَهُودِيًّا وَلا نَصْرانِيًّا وَلكِنْ كانَ حَنِيفاً مُسْلِماً [Āl ʿImrān: 67], meaning by «الحنيف» the one who performs the pilgrimage. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: You claim that Ibrāhīm was one of you, yet Ibrāhīm used to perform the pilgrimage.
Abū Jaʿfar said: «الحنيف» in the language is: the front of one foot turning towards the other by a natural formation that does not go away; so the meaning of «الحنيف» among the Arabs is one who inclines to Islam in truth. As for His, Majestic and Mighty, informing about Ibrāhīm ﷺ that he was a Muslim, that is clear; and it is known that he was a Muslim — he and all the prophets and the righteous — by knowing what Islam is and what faith (īmān) is. It is one of the foundations of the religion, of which ignorance is not excusable, and knowledge of it comes from the language. Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning of «مسلم» in the language is: humbled to the command of Allah, submissive to it; and the meaning of «مؤمن» is: one who confirms what has come from Allah, accepting it and acting upon it at all times. And this is something that cannot be denied to be the religion of every prophet, angel and righteous person.

nahhas-irab:68-68.t: (إِنَّ أَوْلَى النَّاسِ بِإِبْراهِيمَ لَلَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوهُ): the ism of «إنّ» and its khabar. (وَهذَا النَّبِيُّ) is conjoined to «الذين»; «وهذا النبيَّ» in the accusative is also permissible, conjoining it to the hāʾ (in «اتبعوه»).

nahhas-irab:69-69.t: (وَما يُضِلُّونَ إِلَّا أَنْفُسَهُمْ وَما يَشْعُرُونَ): it may be asked: is this an excuse for them? There are two answers to this, the sum of which is that they have no excuse. It has been said: the meaning of «لا يشعرون» is that they do not know the soundness of Islam, though it is incumbent on them to know, because the proofs are manifest and the arguments dazzling. Another answer is that they do not perceive that they will not succeed in leading the believers astray.

nahhas-irab:71-71.t: «وتكتموا الحق» (in the accusative) is also permissible, as the answer to the question.

nahhas-irab:72-72.t: (وَقالَتْ طائِفَةٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتابِ آمِنُوا بِالَّذِي أُنْزِلَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَجْهَ النَّهارِ): as an adverbial (ẓarf), and likewise (آخِرَهُ). The doctrine of Qatāda is that they did this to make the Muslims doubt. It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: The Jews saw the Prophet ﷺ praying the dawn prayer towards Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis), their qibla, and that pleased them; then the qibla was turned towards the Kaaba in the noon prayer, so the Jews said: «Believe in what was sent down upon those who believe at the beginning of the day» — meaning the dawn prayer, when he prayed towards Jerusalem — (وَاكْفُرُوا آخِرَهُ) — meaning the noon prayer, when he prayed towards the Kaaba. (لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ), i.e. to your qibla.

nahhas-irab:73-73.t: (وَلا تُؤْمِنُوا إِلَّا لِمَنْ تَبِعَ دِينَكُمْ): Abū Jaʿfar said: this verse is among the most difficult in the sūra; we have already mentioned it, and the iʿrāb clarifies it. There are several views on it. Whoever says that there is a fronting and a postponing (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr) in the speech, then the meaning is: «and do not believe that anyone will be given the like of what you were given except one who follows your religion», and he makes the lām redundant (zāʾida), so for him it is an exception not of the same kind as the first, otherwise the fronting would not be permitted. Whoever says that the meaning involves no fronting or postponing likewise makes the lām redundant, or attached to a maṣdar, i.e. «do not make your affirmation except for one who follows your religion, that anyone will be given knowledge of the message of the Prophet ﷺ like what you were given»; and a third implied construction is: «out of dislike that anyone should be given the like of what you were given». Al-Farrāʾ said: it is possible that the speech of the Jews ended at His saying «إلّا لمن تبع دينكم», and then He said to Muḥammad ﷺ (قُلْ إِنَّ الْهُدى هُدَى اللَّهِ), i.e. the clarification is Allah's clarification «أن يؤتى أحد مثل ما أوتيتم», i.e. He has made clear that no one will be given the like of what you were given; and «أحد» is valid here because «أن» has the meaning of «لا», as in يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَضِلُّوا [al-Nisāʾ: 176], i.e. «أن لا تضلّوا» (lest you go astray). Abū Jaʿfar said: regarding His saying (قُلْ إِنَّ الْهُدى هُدَى اللَّهِ) there are two views. One of them is that guidance to good and indication of Allah are in the hand of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, who gives it to His prophets, so do not deny that anyone other than you should be given the like of what you were given; and if they deny that, then say: bounty is in the hand of Allah, He gives it to whom He wills. The other view is: say, guidance is the guidance of Allah which He has given the believers, of affirming Muḥammad ﷺ, not anything else — that anyone should be given the like of what you were given of proofs, arguments and reports of what is in their books, or that they should argue with you before your Lord. Al-Akhfash said: i.e. «and do not believe that anyone will be given the like of what you were given, and do not believe that they will argue with you»; he takes the view that it is conjoined. Al-Farrāʾ said: «أو» has the meaning of «حتّى» (until) and «إلّا أن» (unless).

nahhas-irab:75-75.t: (وَمِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتابِ مَنْ إِنْ تَأْمَنْهُ بِقِنْطارٍ): Abū al-Ashhab read «من إن تيمنه». «من» is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), or by the adjective (ṣifa); the condition and its apodosis are its ṣila (relative clause) according to the Basrans, and according to the Kufans with an implied «القول» (saying). «تيمنه» is according to the dialect of those who say «تستعين» [Translator's note: i.e. those who give the prefix of the imperfect a kasra, «تِئمنه» > «تيمنه»; the example as printed is unvowelled]. In (يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ) there are five ways, four of which have been read. The best of them is the reading of Nāfiʿ and al-Kisāʾī «يؤدّهي إليك», with a yāʾ in continuous reading (al-idrāj). Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ read يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ with kasra on the hāʾ, without yāʾ. Abū al-Mundhir Sallām read يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ with ḍamma on the hāʾ, without wāw, and he read its sisters likewise, such as نُوَلِّهِ ما تَوَلَّى [al-Nisāʾ: 115], «عليه» and «إليه». Abū ʿUbayd said: Abū ʿAmr, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza agreed on stopping the hāʾ (with sukūn), and read it يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ [Translator's note: the printed vowelling of these variant readings does not reproduce the differences being described]. Abū Jaʿfar said: the fifth way is «يؤدّهو إليك», with a wāw in continuous reading; this is the original, because the hāʾ is faint (khafiyya). Al-Khalīl claimed that it was reinforced with a strong letter, which is the wāw. Someone else said: the wāw was chosen for it because the wāw is from the lips and the hāʾ has a distant place of articulation. Sībawayh said: the wāw in the masculine is like the alif in the feminine, and a yāʾ is substituted for it, because the yāʾ is lighter, when a kasra or a yāʾ precedes it. The yāʾ is dropped and the kasra remains because the yāʾ used to be dropped and the verb is nominative, so it was kept as it was. Whoever says «يؤدّهُ إليك» has as his argument that he dropped the wāw and kept the ḍamma, just as it was when nominative too. As for giving the hāʾ a sukūn, it is not permitted except in poetry, according to some grammarians, while some of them permit it; and Abū ʿAmr is too eminent for something like this to be allowed of him; what is sound from him is that he used to give the hāʾ a kasra. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and al-Aʿmash read (إِلَّا ما دُمْتَ) with kasra on the dāl, from «دِمت تدام», like «خفت تخاف», the dialect of Azd al-Sarāt; and al-Akhfash related «دِمت تدوم» as anomalous (shādhdh). (ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ), i.e. their doing that, and their affair is that, because they (قالُوا لَيْسَ عَلَيْنا فِي الْأُمِّيِّينَ سَبِيلٌ), i.e. a way of wrongdoing.

nahhas-irab:76-76.t:
Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: (بَلى),
i.e. yes indeed, there is against them a way of punishment because of their lying and their declaring [it] lawful. Abū Isḥāq said: the statement is complete here; then He said (مَنْ أَوْفى بِعَهْدِهِ وَاتَّقى). Abū Jaʿfar said: (مَنْ) is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and it is conditional; (أَوْفى) is in the position of the jussive, and (وَاتَّقى) is conjoined to it, i.e. and fears Allah, and so does not lie and does not declare lawful what has been forbidden to him. (فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُتَّقِينَ), i.e. He loves those.

nahhas-irab:77-77.t: (الَّذِينَ) is the ism [of «إنّ»], and (أُولئِكَ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), what follows it is its khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of «إنّ». (وَلا يُكَلِّمُهُمُ اللَّهُ): we have already mentioned its meaning, and we explain it further. The meaning is: Allah will not let them hear His speech without an intermediary, as Allah spoke to Mūsā ﷺ; so this is its meaning: He will not speak to them in reality, but He speaks to them figuratively, by commanding the angels to bring them to account, as He said فَوَ رَبِّكَ لَنَسْئَلَنَّهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ عَمَّا كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ [al-Ḥijr: 92, 93], and likewise أَيْنَ شُرَكائِيَ [al-Naḥl: 27]; so when the angels say to them «Allah says to you such-and-such», He has spoken to them figuratively. It has been said that the meaning of «لا يكلّمهم» is: He will be angry with them. And it has been said: the meaning is figurative, i.e. He will not speak to them the speech of one pleased with them, but the speech of one rebuking them, making them confess and holding them to account. (وَلا يَنْظُرُ إِلَيْهِمْ), with His mercy, and will not give them any good, as one says: so-and-so does not look at his child.

nahhas-irab:78-78.t: (وَإِنَّ مِنْهُمْ لَفَرِيقاً): the ism of «إنّ», and the lām is for emphasis (tawkīd). (يَلْوُونَ أَلْسِنَتَهُمْ): Abū Jaʿfar and Shayba read «يلوّون ألسنتهم», [the intensive form] for multiplicity. Ḥumayd ibn Qays read «يلون ألسنتهم»; its underlying form is «يلوون», then he gave the wāw a hamza because of its ḍamma, then lightened the hamza and threw its vowel onto what precedes it. «ألسنة» is the plural of «لسان» in the dialect of those who treat it as masculine; those who treat it as feminine say «ألسن».

nahhas-irab:79-79.t: (ما كانَ لِبَشَرٍ أَنْ يُؤْتِيَهُ): accusative by «أن». (ثُمَّ يَقُولَ) is conjoined to it. Maḥbūb related from Abū ʿAmr «ثم يقولُ» in the nominative; the accusative is better. (وَلكِنْ كُونُوا رَبَّانِيِّينَ): the saying (al-qawl) is omitted, and the implied construction is «ولكن يقول» (but he says). ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān [al-Akhfash the younger] said: the meaning is «ولكن ليقل» (but let him say); and the wāw enters upon «لكن» while both are conjunctions, according to the view of some, because of the weakness of «لكن». Ibn Kaysān said: the wāw is the conjunction and «لكن» is for affirmation. (بِما كُنْتُمْ تُعَلِّمُونَ الْكِتابَ): this is the reading of Abū ʿAmr and the people of Medina [Translator's note: presumably «تَعْلَمون», without the doubling]; Ibn ʿAbbās and the people of Kufa read تُعَلِّمُونَ with ḍamma on the tāʾ and a doubled lām; and Mujāhid read «تعلّمون» with fatḥa on the tāʾ and a doubled lām, i.e. «تتعلّمون» (you learn) and they study. Abū ʿUbayd was opposed in this choice, because Shuʿba related from ʿĀṣim, from Zayd [Translator's note: presumably Zirr], from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: وَلكِنْ كُونُوا رَبَّانِيِّينَ — he said: wise men, scholars. And al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: no one should abandon memorising the Qur'an as far as he is able, for Allah, Majestic and Mighty, says: وَلكِنْ كُونُوا رَبَّانِيِّينَ بِما كُنْتُمْ تُعَلِّمُونَ الْكِتابَ وَبِما كُنْتُمْ تَدْرُسُونَ, i.e. jurists, scholars. So it has been said: it is unlikely that one would say «be wise men and scholars by your teaching», whereas it is good to say: «be wise men and scholars by your knowledge».

nahhas-irab:80-80.t: Sībawayh said: (وَلا يَأْمُرَكُمْ) came cut off from the first, because he meant «ولا يأمركم الله» (and Allah does not command you). Al-Akhfash said: i.e. «وهو لا يأمركم» (and He does not command you). This [the nominative] is the reading of Abū ʿAmr, al-Kisāʾī and the people of the two Sanctuaries; as for al-Yazīdī's report from Abū ʿAmr that he gave the rāʾ a sukūn, that is an error. Sībawayh said: some read وَلا يَأْمُرَكُمْ [in the accusative] on the basis of His saying ما كانَ لِبَشَرٍ أَنْ يُؤْتِيَهُ اللَّهُ [Āl ʿImrān: 79]. Abū Jaʿfar said: the accusative is the reading of Ibn Abī Isḥāq, Ḥamza and ʿĀṣim. (أَنْ تَتَّخِذُوا), i.e. «بأن تتخذوا». (الْمَلائِكَةَ وَالنَّبِيِّينَ أَرْباباً): this is found among the Christians: they venerate the angels and the prophets until they make them lords. They relate from Sulaymān ﷺ that he said: «My Lord said to my Lord: sit at my right hand», by which they mean: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said to the Messiah ﷺ.

nahhas-irab:81-81.t: I.e. «واذكر» (and remember). Sībawayh said: I asked al-Khalīl about His saying, Majestic and Mighty, وَإِذْ أَخَذَ اللَّهُ مِيثاقَ النَّبِيِّينَ, and he said: «ما» has the meaning of «الذي» (that which). Abū Jaʿfar said: the implied construction according to al-Khalīl's view is «للذي آتيتكموه» (for that which I have given you); then the hāʾ was dropped because of the length of the noun. So «الذي» is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is (مِنْ كِتابٍ وَحِكْمَةٍ), with «من» for clarifying the genus; al-Akhfash said: it is redundant (zāʾida). The khabar may also be (لَتُؤْمِنُنَّ بِهِ). Al-Kisāʾī said: «ما» is conditional, so according to his view its position is accusative by «آتيتكم». The people of Kufa read لَما آتَيْتُكُمْ with kasra on the lām [«لِما»], and al-Farrāʾ said: i.e. He took the covenant for what He gave them of Book and wisdom, and he made «لتؤمننّ به» part of the taking of the covenant, as you say: «أخذت ميثاقك لتفعلنّ» (I took your covenant that you will surely do). Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū ʿUbayda has a good view on this. He said: the meaning is «and when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Book: you shall surely believe in him, because of what I have given you of mention of him in the Torah». It has also been said: there is an ellipsis in the speech, and the meaning is «and when Allah took the covenant of the prophets: you shall surely teach people what has come to you of Book and wisdom, and you shall surely bind people to believe»; and this ellipsis is indicated by (وَأَخَذْتُمْ عَلى ذلِكُمْ إِصْرِي).

nahhas-irab:82-82.t: (فَمَنْ تَوَلَّى بَعْدَ ذلِكَ): a condition, and the meaning is: whoever turns away from faith after the taking of the covenant; and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is (فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْفاسِقُونَ).

nahhas-irab:83-83.t: (أَفَغَيْرَ دِينِ اللَّهِ يَبْغُونَ): «غير» is made accusative by «يبغون». (وَلَهُ أَسْلَمَ مَنْ فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ): if you wish, you may assimilate the mīm into the mīm. We have already mentioned two views on its meaning. The first of them is that the meaning is: to Him whoever is in the heavens and the earth has submitted and been humbled, as you say: «أسلم فلان نفسه للموت» (so-and-so surrendered himself to death). So the meaning is that Allah, Majestic and Mighty, created creation as He willed: among them are the handsome and the ugly, the tall and the short, the healthy and the sick, and all of them are compliant by compulsion; the healthy one is compliant, obedient and loving that, and the sick one is compliant and submissive even if he dislikes it. (طَوْعاً وَكَرْهاً): a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. obedient and compelled.

nahhas-irab:84-84.t: (قُلْ آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ): there are three answers on this. «قل» may have the meaning of «قولوا» (say, plural), because addressing the Prophet ﷺ is addressing his community; the meaning may be «say to them: say, we believe in Allah»; and what is meant may be the community, and its parallel is يا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ إِذا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّساءَ [al-Ṭalāq: 1].

nahhas-irab:85-85.t: (وَمَنْ يَبْتَغِ): a condition, and for that reason the yāʾ has been dropped from it; and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is (فَلَنْ يُقْبَلَ مِنْهُ). Abū Ḥātim claimed that Abū ʿAmr and al-Aʿmash read وَمَنْ يَبْتَغِ غَيْرَ الْإِسْلامِ دِيناً with assimilation [of the ghayn into the ghayn]. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is not good, because of the kasra that is on the ghayn. (وَهُوَ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنَ الْخاسِرِينَ): Hishām said: i.e. «and he is a loser in the Hereafter, one of the losers»; were it not for this, you would have separated the ṣila (relative clause) from the relative. Al-Māzinī said: the alif and lām [in «الخاسرين»] are like those in «الرجل» (i.e. the definite article, not a relative). Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: the adverbial phrase is attached to an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun).

nahhas-irab:86-86.t: (كَيْفَ يَهْدِي اللَّهُ قَوْماً كَفَرُوا بَعْدَ إِيمانِهِمْ): the ḍamma was dropped from the yāʾ because of its heaviness, and the yāʾ was dropped from pronunciation because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, but it was kept in writing because writing follows the pause form.

nahhas-irab:90-90.t: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بَعْدَ إِيمانِهِمْ): the ism of «إنّ», and the khabar (predicate) is (لَنْ تُقْبَلَ تَوْبَتُهُمْ). We have mentioned several views on its meaning. It has also been said about it that the meaning is: those who disbelieve after their faith and then increase in disbelief, their repentance will not be accepted at death. Abū Jaʿfar said: this view is good, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: وَلَيْسَتِ التَّوْبَةُ لِلَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ السَّيِّئاتِ حَتَّى إِذا حَضَرَ أَحَدَهُمُ الْمَوْتُ قالَ إِنِّي تُبْتُ الْآنَ [al-Nisāʾ: 18]. It has also been said: their repentance which they had before they disbelieved will not be accepted, because disbelief has nullified it. Abū Jaʿfar said: ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān narrated to us: Abū Saʿīd al-Sukkarī narrated to us: Muḥammad ibn Ḥabīb narrated to us: Muḥammad ibn al-Mustanīr — who is Quṭrub — narrated to us, concerning the saying of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بَعْدَ إِيمانِهِمْ ثُمَّ ازْدادُوا كُفْراً لَنْ تُقْبَلَ تَوْبَتُهُمْ, while Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has said in another place وَهُوَ الَّذِي يَقْبَلُ التَّوْبَةَ عَنْ عِبادِهِ [al-Shūrā: 25]: this verse concerns some people of Mecca who said: we will wait for the misfortune of fate to befall Muḥammad ﷺ, and if it seems good to us to return, we will return to our people. So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, revealed إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بَعْدَ إِيمانِهِمْ ثُمَّ ازْدادُوا كُفْراً لَنْ تُقْبَلَ تَوْبَتُهُمْ, i.e. their repentance will not be accepted while they persist in disbelief. He called it a repentance that is not accepted because no firm resolve was sound on the part of those people; and Allah, Majestic and Mighty, accepts all repentance when the resolve is sound.

nahhas-irab:91-91.t:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَماتُوا وَهُمْ كُفَّارٌ): the ism of «إنّ», and the khabar (predicate) is (فَلَنْ يُقْبَلَ مِنْ أَحَدِهِمْ مِلْءُ الْأَرْضِ ذَهَباً). [«ذهبا»] is accusative as clarification (al-bayān, i.e. tamyīz). Al-Farrāʾ said: its nominative is permissible as a new start (al-istiʾnāf), as though he meant «هو ذهب» (it is gold). Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā [Thaʿlab] said: the nominative is permissible as a clarification of «ملء».
The third part of the book Iʿrāb al-Qurʾān is completed. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and blessings upon Muḥammad the trustworthy and upon all his family.

nahhas-irab:92-92.t: (لَنْ تَنالُوا): accusative by «لن», and the sign of the accusative is the dropping of the nūn; and likewise (حَتَّى تُنْفِقُوا).

nahhas-irab:93-93.t:
(كُلُّ الطَّعامِ): mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is (كانَ حِلًّا). One says «حلّ» and «حلال», «حرم» and «حرام».
(إِلَّا ما حَرَّمَ إِسْرائِيلُ عَلى نَفْسِهِ): an exception.

nahhas-irab:95-95.t:
ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said:
(حَنِيفاً) is in the sense of «أعني» (I mean) [i.e. accusative by an implied «أعني»].

nahhas-irab:96-96.t: (إِنَّ أَوَّلَ بَيْتٍ): the ism of «إنّ», and the khabar (predicate) is (لَلَّذِي بِبَكَّةَ), and the lām is for emphasis (tawkīd). (مُبارَكاً): as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Outside the Qur'an «مباركٌ» would be permissible, as a second khabar, as a badal (substitute) from «الذي», or with an implied mubtadaʾ (subject). (وَهُدىً لِلْعالَمِينَ) is conjoined to it, and it may have the meaning of «وهو هدى للعالمين» (and it is guidance for the worlds). The meaning is: the first house set up for people as blessed and as guidance for the worlds is the one at Bakka — as it is related from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he was asked about it: Is it the first house set up for people? He said: No; Nūḥ ﷺ and his people were in houses before Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him), but it is the first house in which blessing was placed. Outside the Qur'an «مباركٍ» in the genitive would be permissible, as a naʿt (adjective) of «بيت». [Translator's note: the printed text has «ببدكة» in the paraphrase, presumably a misprint for «ببكة».]

nahhas-irab:97-97.t:
فِيهِ آياتٌ بَيِّناتٌ مَقامُ إِبْراهِيمَ وَمَنْ دَخَلَهُ كانَ آمِناً وَلِلَّهِ عَلَى النَّاسِ حِجُّ الْبَيْتِ مَنِ اسْتَطاعَ إِلَيْهِ سَبِيلاً وَمَنْ كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ عَنِ الْعالَمِينَ (97) (فِيهِ آياتٌ بَيِّناتٌ): nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), or by the adjectival phrase (al-ṣifa). (مقام إبراهيم): there are three ways for its nominative.
Al-Akhfash said: i.e. «منها مقام إبراهيم» (among them is the station of Ibrāhīm). It is related from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] that he said: «مقام» is a badal (substitute) from «آيات». The third view is in the sense of «هي مقام إبراهيم» (they are the station of Ibrāhīm). Al-Akhfash's view is well known in the speech of the Arabs, as Zuhayr said: [al-Basīṭ] 79-
لها متاع وأعوان غدون لها ... قتب وغرب إذا ما أفرغ انسحقا
(It has gear and helpers who go out early for it: a saddle-frame and a large bucket which, whenever it is emptied, pours out.)
And the view of Abū al-ʿAbbās [al-Mubarrad] is that «مقاما» has the meaning of «مقامات» (stations), because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun); Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said خَتَمَ اللَّهُ عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ وَعَلى سَمْعِهِمْ [al-Baqara: 7], and Jarīr said: [al-Basīṭ] 80-
إنّ العيون التي في طرفها مرض ... قتلننا ثمّ لم يحيين قتلانا
(The eyes in whose glance there is languor have slain us, then have not revived our slain.)
This is strengthened by the ḥadīth that is related: «The whole of the pilgrimage is the station of Ibrāhīm». (وَمَنْ دَخَلَهُ كانَ آمِناً): it may be conjoined to «مقام», i.e. «and in it are signs: whoever enters it is safe», because that is among the signs: people used to be snatched away all around the Sanctuary, yet when a king aimed at it, he perished. (مَنْ) may also be nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with the khabar (predicate) (كانَ آمِناً). (وَلِلَّهِ عَلَى النَّاسِ حِجُّ الْبَيْتِ مَنِ اسْتَطاعَ إِلَيْهِ سَبِيلًا): (مَنْ) is in the position of the genitive as a badal of the part from the whole; this is the view of most grammarians. Al-Kisāʾī permitted «من» to be in the position of the nominative, with (اسْتَطاعَ) as a condition and the apodosis omitted, i.e. «whoever is able to find a way to it, the pilgrimage is incumbent on him».

nahhas-irab:98-98.t: (قُلْ يا أَهْلَ الْكِتابِ لِمَ تَكْفُرُونَ بِآياتِ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ شَهِيدٌ عَلى ما تَعْمَلُونَ), and before this [He said] وَأَنْتُمْ تَشْهَدُونَ [Āl ʿImrān: 70]; so Allah is a witness against them, and they bear witness against themselves to disbelief in the signs of Allah, when the proofs have become manifest.

nahhas-irab:99-99.t: (لِمَ تَصُدُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ مَنْ آمَنَ تَبْغُونَها عِوَجاً), i.e. «تبغون لها» (you seek for it [crookedness]), and the lām was dropped, like وَإِذا كالُوهُمْ [al-Muṭaffifīn: 3], i.e. «كالوا لهم» (they measured for them). One says «بغيت له كذا» (I sought such-and-such for him) and «أبغيته» (I helped him seek it). (وَأَنْتُمْ شُهَداءُ): it has been said: this is for those who recognise him as they recognise their own sons; and it has been said: «شهداء» means knowing that it is the way of Allah.

nahhas-irab:100-100.t: (إِنْ تُطِيعُوا فَرِيقاً): a condition, and for that reason the nūn has been dropped from it; and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is (يَرُدُّوكُمْ بَعْدَ إِيمانِكُمْ كافِرِينَ).

nahhas-irab:101-101.t:
(وَكَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ): (كَيْفَ) is in the position of the accusative. The fāʾ is given a fatḥa, according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the fatḥa was chosen for it because before the fāʾ there is a yāʾ, and it was heavy for them to combine a yāʾ and a kasra.
The Kufans said: when two quiescent letters meet within one word, one of them takes a fatḥa, and when they are in two words, a kasra. (وَأَنْتُمْ تُتْلى عَلَيْكُمْ آياتُ اللَّهِ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَفِيكُمْ رَسُولُهُ): nominative as a mubtadaʾ, or if you wish by the adjectival phrase, according to the view of al-Kisāʾī. (وَمَنْ يَعْتَصِمْ بِاللَّهِ): a condition, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is (فَقَدْ هُدِيَ إِلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ).

nahhas-irab:102-102.t: (يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقاتِهِ): a maṣdar (verbal noun). The origin of «تقاة» is «تقية»; the yāʾ was changed to an alif, and the tāʾ is changed from a wāw, because it is from «وقى». You may also bring the wāw and say «وقاة», and if you wish you may replace the wāw with a hamza and say «أقاة», like «أقّتت». We have already mentioned (وَلا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ).

nahhas-irab:103-103.t:
(وَاعْتَصِمُوا بِحَبْلِ اللَّهِ): one says «اعتصمت بفلان» and «اعتصمت فلانا» (I held fast to so-and-so), and the meaning is: hold fast to the Qur'an against disbelief and falsehood. (جَمِيعاً): as a ḥāl (circumstantial), according to Sībawayh. (وَلا تَفَرَّقُوا): a prohibition, and for that reason the nūn has been dropped from it; the origin is «تتفرّقوا», and it has been read وَلا تَفَرَّقُوا with assimilation of the tāʾ into the tāʾ.
(فَأَصْبَحْتُمْ بِنِعْمَتِهِ إِخْواناً): the khabar of «أصبح». One also says «أخوان», like «حملان». The origin of «أخ» is «أخو», and the evidence for this is their saying in the dual «أخوان»; it should have been said «مررت باخا» as one says «مررت بعصا», except that it was dropped from it by analogy with something else; and Hishām related: «مكره أخاك لا بطل» (your brother is compelled, not a hero).
(وَكُنْتُمْ عَلى شَفا حُفْرَةٍ مِنَ النَّارِ): the origin of «شفا» is «شفو», and for this reason it is written with alif and is not pronounced with imāla.
(فَأَنْقَذَكُمْ مِنْها): the hāʾ refers back to the Fire, because it is what is intended, or to the pit, i.e. He saved you from it through the Prophet ﷺ.

nahhas-irab:104-104.t: (وَلْتَكُنْ): an imperative. The origin is «ولِتكونُ»; the kasra was dropped because of its heaviness, the ḍamma was dropped from the nūn for the jussive, and the wāw was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. (أُمَّةٌ): the ism of «تكن». (يَدْعُونَ إِلَى الْخَيْرِ) is in the position of a naʿt (adjective), and what follows it is conjoined to it.

nahhas-irab:105-105.t: (وَلا تَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ تَفَرَّقُوا): the kāf is in the position of the accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf), and it is in the position of the khabar (predicate). Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh said: (كَالَّذِينَ تَفَرَّقُوا وَاخْتَلَفُوا مِنْ بَعْدِ ما جاءَهُمُ الْبَيِّناتُ) are the Jews and the Christians. «جاءهم» is masculine on the basis of the plural (al-jamīʿ), and «جاءتهم» on the basis of the group (al-jamāʿa).

nahhas-irab:106-106.t: (يَوْمَ تَبْيَضُّ وُجُوهٌ وَتَسْوَدُّ وُجُوهٌ): «تِبيضّ» and «تِسودّ» with kasra on the tāʾ are also permissible, because you say «ابيضّت», so you give the tāʾ a kasra as you give the alif a kasra. «تبياضّ» is also permissible, and it has been read so, and kasra on the tāʾ in it is also permissible. «يوم يبيّض وجوه» is permissible, treating the plural as masculine, and «أجوه» is permissible, like «أقّتت». (فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ اسْوَدَّتْ وُجُوهُهُمْ): nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and we have already mentioned it.

nahhas-irab:107-107.t: (وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ ابْيَضَّتْ وُجُوهُهُمْ): mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is (فَفِي رَحْمَتِ اللَّهِ). (هُمْ فِيها خالِدُونَ): «هم» may be redundant (zāʾida), or it may be a mubtadaʾ; and outside the Qur'an the accusative «خالدين» is permissible, as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:108-108.t: (تِلْكَ آياتُ اللَّهِ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), i.e. those things mentioned are the proofs and indications of Allah, Majestic and Mighty. «آيات الله» may also be a badal (substitute) from «تلك», but it cannot be a naʿt (adjective): a vague noun (al-mubham, the demonstrative) is not qualified by a muḍāf (annexed noun).

nahhas-irab:110-110.t:
(كُنْتُمْ خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ): «كنتم» may be redundant (zāʾida), i.e. «أنتم خير أمّة» (you are the best community), and Sībawayh recited: [al-Wāfir] 81-
وجيران لنا كانوا كرام
(And neighbours of ours who were noble.)
It may also mean: you were, in the Preserved Tablet, the best community. Sufyān related from Maysara al-Ashjaʿī, from Abū Ḥāzim, from Abū Hurayra: (كُنْتُمْ خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ أُخْرِجَتْ لِلنَّاسِ) — he said: you drag people in chains to Islam. So the implied construction on this basis is: you were the best community. According to the view of Mujāhid: you were the best community when you enjoined right and forbade wrong. It has been said: the community of Muḥammad ﷺ became the best community only because the Muslims among them enjoined right most, and forbidding wrong is most widespread among them. And it has been said: this is for the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, as the Prophet ﷺ said: «The best of people is my generation, those among whom I was sent».

nahhas-irab:111-111.t:
(لَنْ يَضُرُّوكُمْ): accusative by «لن», and the statement is complete. (إِلَّا أَذىً): an exception not of the same kind as the first.
(وَإِنْ يُقاتِلُوكُمْ يُوَلُّوكُمُ الْأَدْبارَ): a condition and its apodosis, and the statement is complete. (ثُمَّ لا يُنْصَرُونَ) is resumptive (mustaʾnaf), and for that reason the nūn is retained in it.

nahhas-irab:112-112.t: (ضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الذِّلَّةُ أَيْنَ ما ثُقِفُوا): the statement is complete. (إِلَّا بِحَبْلٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ): an exception not of the same kind as the first, i.e. but they hold fast to a rope from Allah, which is the covenant.

nahhas-irab:113-113.t:
(لَيْسُوا سَواءً): the statement is complete. (مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتابِ أُمَّةٌ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), except that al-Farrāʾ has a view on it: he claimed that «أمة» is made nominative by «سواء», and its implied construction is «ليس تستوي أمة من أهل الكتاب قائمة يتلون آيات الله وأمة كافرة» (not equal are a community of the People of the Book upright, reciting the signs of Allah, and a disbelieving community). Abū Jaʿfar said: this view is wrong in several respects. One of them is that he makes «أمة» nominative by «سواء», so that nothing refers back to the ism of «ليس»; he makes [a noun] nominative by something that does not function like the verb; and he implies something that is not needed, because mention of the disbelievers has already preceded, so there is no reason to imply this. Abū ʿUbayda said: this is like their saying «أكلوني البراغيث» (the fleas ate me); this is an error, because mention of them has already preceded, while in «أكلوني البراغيث» there has been no prior mention of them. Ibn ʿAbbās said: (مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتابِ أُمَّةٌ قائِمَةٌ يَتْلُونَ آياتِ اللَّهِ) are those who believed along with the Prophet ﷺ. Al-Akhfash said: the implied construction is «من أهل الكتاب ذو أمة», i.e. one possessing a good way (ṭarīqa), and he recited:
[al-Ṭawīl] 82-
وهل يأثمن ذو أمّة وهو طائع
(And would one who holds to a [right] way commit sin while obedient?)
(آناءَ اللَّيْلِ): an adverbial of time.

nahhas-irab:114-114.t: (يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ): it may be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); it may be in the position of a naʿt (adjective) of «أمة»; and it may be resumptive (mustaʾnaf); and what follows it is conjoined to it.

nahhas-irab:116-117.t: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا): the ism of «إنّ», and the khabar (predicate) is (لَنْ تُغْنِيَ عَنْهُمْ أَمْوالُهُمْ وَلا أَوْلادُهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئاً). (وَأُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ النَّارِ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar, and likewise (هُمْ فِيها خالِدُونَ), and likewise (مَثَلُ ما يُنْفِقُونَ فِي هذِهِ الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا كَمَثَلِ رِيحٍ) [Translator's note: the printed text runs these words together as «وكذاثَلُ»]; the implied construction is «كمثل مهلك ريح» (like the destruction wrought by a wind). Ibn ʿAbbās said: «الصرّ» is intense cold.

nahhas-irab:118-118.t: (يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَتَّخِذُوا بِطانَةً مِنْ دُونِكُمْ): al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: they are the disbelievers and the hypocrites. Abū Jaʿfar said: there are two views on it. One of them is that (مِنْ دُونِكُمْ) means «من سواكم» (from other than you); al-Farrāʾ said: وَيَعْمَلُونَ عَمَلًا دُونَ ذلِكَ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 82], i.e. other than that. The other view is: do not take as intimates those who are below you in decency and soundness of doctrine. This indicates that it is incumbent on the people of the Sunna to keep away from the people of whims (ahl al-ahwāʾ) and to abandon mixing with them, because they have no scruples about deceiving them. Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: لا يَأْلُونَكُمْ خَبالًا وَدُّوا ما عَنِتُّمْ to the end of the verse.

nahhas-irab:119-119.t:
(ها أَنْتُمْ أُولاءِ تُحِبُّونَهُمْ وَلا يُحِبُّونَكُمْ): al-Farrāʾ claimed that when the Arabs bring a pronoun (ism mukannā) and intend «al-taqrīb» (the deictic-copular use), they separate between «ها» and the noun pointed at by the pronoun: a man says to another «أين أنت؟» (where are you?), and he says «ها أنا ذا» (here I am); and according to him this is permissible only in taqrīb and with the pronoun. Abū Isḥāq said: it is permissible with the pronoun and with the overt noun, except that it is more frequent with the pronoun. Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said: «ها أنتم» — its origin is «أاأنتم», with two hamzas with an alif between them, as Dhū al-Rumma said: [al-Ṭawīl] 83-
أاأنت أم أمّ سالم
(Is it you, or Umm Sālim?)
Then it was heavy, so they replaced the hamza with a hāʾ. (ها أَنْتُمْ) is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (أُولاءِ) is the khabar (predicate); (تُحِبُّونَهُمْ) is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). «أولاء» takes a kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. «أولاء» may also have the meaning of «الذين» (who), with «تحبّونهم» as its ṣila (relative clause). (وَلا يُحِبُّونَكُمْ وَتُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْكِتابِ كُلِّهِ): conjoined; and «الكتاب» has the meaning of «الكتب» (the books).

nahhas-irab:120-120.t:
(إِنْ تَمْسَسْكُمْ حَسَنَةٌ): a condition. (تَسُؤْهُمْ): the requital (mujāzāt, i.e. the apodosis). And likewise (وَإِنْ تَصْبِرُوا وَتَتَّقُوا لا يَضُرُّكُمْ كَيْدُهُمْ شَيْئاً) [Translator's note: in the variant being explained here, presumably «لا يَضِرْكُم»]: the yāʾ was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, because when you dropped the ḍamma from the rāʾ, the rāʾ remained quiescent and the yāʾ quiescent, so the yāʾ was dropped, and it was the more deserving of being dropped because before it is something that indicates it. Al-Kisāʾī related that he heard «ضاره يضوره», and he permitted لا يَضُرُّكُمْ [Translator's note: presumably «لا يَضُرْكُم»], and claimed that in the reading of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb it is «لا يضرركم»; so these are three ways. The Kufans read لا يَضُرُّكُمْ كَيْدُهُمْ شَيْئاً with ḍamma on the rāʾ and its doubling. In this there are three ways, and all three are weak. One of them is that it is in the position of the jussive, and given a ḍamma because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and they chose the ḍamma — and there are three ways in it — on account of the ḍamma of the ḍād; this is far-fetched, because it resembles the nominative, and the ḍamma is heavy. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ claimed that it is with an implied fāʾ, as the poet said:
[al-Basīṭ] 84-
من يفعل الحسنات الله يشكرها ... والشرّ بالشرّ عند الله مثلان
(Whoever does good deeds, Allah will reward them; and evil for evil, with Allah, are two equals.)
A third implied construction is: «لا يضرّكم أن تصبروا» (it will not harm you, if you are patient) [i.e. the apodosis is fronted]; and Sībawayh recited: [al-Rajaz] 85-
إنّك إن يصرع أخوك تصرع
(Truly, if your brother is thrown down, you will be thrown down.)
Al-Farrāʾ claimed that it is by fronting and postponing (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr). Al-Mufaḍḍal al-Ḍabbī related from ʿĀṣim لا يَضُرُّكُمْ with fatḥa on the rāʾ, because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, owing to the lightness of the fatḥa. The sixth way is لا يَضُرُّكُمْ with kasra on the rāʾ, because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.

nahhas-irab:121-121.t:
(وَإِذْ غَدَوْتَ مِنْ أَهْلِكَ تُبَوِّئُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ مَقاعِدَ لِلْقِتالِ): Ibn ʿAbbās said: this was on the day of Uḥud.
(إِذْ) is in the position of the accusative, i.e. «اذكر» (remember). Al-Farrāʾ related «وإذي» with a yāʾ, and in the reading of Ibn Masʿūd it is «تبوّى للمؤمنين»; the meaning is the same, i.e. you take for the believers seats and positions. «مقاعد» is a diptote because this plural has no counterpart among singulars, and for this reason it is not itself pluralised. (وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), i.e. hearing what they said, knowing what they conceal.

nahhas-irab:122-122.t: (إِذْ) is in the position of the accusative by «تبوّئ». The maṣdar (verbal noun) [of «همّ»] is «همّا», «مهمّة», «همّة» and «هممًا». (أَنْ تَفْشَلا): accusative by «أن», and for that reason the nūn has been dropped from it. (وَاللَّهُ وَلِيُّهُما): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). (وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ): if you wish, you may give the first lām a kasra, and that is the original. The meaning of «توكّلت على الله» is: I strengthened myself through Him and guarded myself.

nahhas-irab:123-123.t: (وَلَقَدْ نَصَرَكُمُ اللَّهُ بِبَدْرٍ وَأَنْتُمْ أَذِلَّةٌ): the plural of «ذليل». The plural of faʿīl, when it is an adjective, is on the pattern fuʿalāʾ, but they disliked saying «ذللاء» because of its heaviness, so they said «أذلّة», treating it like a noun, such as «رغيف» and «أرغفة» (loaf, loaves).

nahhas-irab:124-124.t: (إِذْ تَقُولُ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ): if you wish, you may assimilate the lām into the lām; and combining two quiescent letters is permissible because one of them is a letter of prolongation and softness.

nahhas-irab:125-125.t:
(بَلى): the statement is complete. (إِنْ تَصْبِرُوا): a condition. (وَتَتَّقُوا وَيَأْتُوكُمْ مِنْ فَوْرِهِمْ): conjoined (nasaq).
(هذا) is a naʿt (adjective) of «فورهم». (يُمْدِدْكُمْ): the apodosis. (بِخَمْسَةِ آلافٍ): the hāʾ (tāʾ marbūṭa) entered because «الألف» (thousand) is masculine.

nahhas-irab:126-126.t: (وَما جَعَلَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَّا بُشْرى لَكُمْ وَلِتَطْمَئِنَّ قُلُوبُكُمْ بِهِ): the lām of kay (purpose), i.e. «and that your hearts might be reassured by it, He made it». (وَمَا النَّصْرُ إِلَّا مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَكِيمِ).

nahhas-irab:127-128.t: (لِيَقْطَعَ طَرَفاً مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا), i.e. by killing; i.e. «that He might cut off a part, [He gave you] your victory»; it may also be attached to «يمددكم». Abū Jaʿfar said: we have already mentioned (أَوْ يَكْبِتَهُمْ أَوْ يَتُوبَ عَلَيْهِمْ).

nahhas-irab:130-130.t: (يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَأْكُلُوا الرِّبَوا أَضْعافاً): a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). (مُضاعَفَةً) is its naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:133-133.t: In the codices of the people of Kufa it is (وَسارِعُوا), conjoining a clause to a clause, and in the codices of the people of Medina it is without wāw, because the meaning is known. (وَجَنَّةٍ عَرْضُهَا السَّماواتُ وَالْأَرْضُ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of the genitive. (أُعِدَّتْ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ).

nahhas-irab:134-134.t:
(الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ فِي السَّرَّاءِ وَالضَّرَّاءِ): a naʿt (adjective) of «المتّقين»; or, if you wish, it is with an implied mubtadaʾ (subject); or, if you wish, you may imply «أعني» (I mean). ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr said: «السرّاء والضرّاء» are ease and hardship.
(وَالْكاظِمِينَ الْغَيْظَ): conjoined; and if you take the first as being in the position of the nominative, this is accusative by «أعني», like يُؤْمِنُونَ بِما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ وَما أُنْزِلَ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ وَالْمُقِيمِينَ الصَّلاةَ [al-Nisāʾ: 162]. (وَالْعافِينَ عَنِ النَّاسِ): conjoined. Abū al-ʿĀliya said: i.e. [pardoning] the slaves.

nahhas-irab:135-135.t: (وَالَّذِينَ إِذا فَعَلُوا فاحِشَةً): conjoined (nasaq). (وَمَنْ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ), i.e. there is no one who forgives disobedience and removes its punishment except Allah, Majestic and Mighty. (وَلَمْ يُصِرُّوا عَلى ما فَعَلُوا وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ): it has been said: i.e. while they know that I punish persistence. And it has been said — and it is a good view — (وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ), i.e. they remember their sins and repent of them; and it is not incumbent on a person, if he does not remember his sin and does not know it, to repent of it specifically, but he should hold the conviction that whenever he remembers a sin he will repent of it.

nahhas-irab:136-136.t:
(أُولئِكَ جَزاؤُهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ): two mubtadaʾs (subjects). (وَجَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ): conjoined (nasaq).
(خالِدِينَ): as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:137-137.t: (قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ سُنَنٌ): «السنّة» in the speech of the Arabs is the straight road; «فلان على السنّة» means he is on the straight road, not inclining to any of the whims (al-ahwāʾ).

nahhas-irab:139-139.t: (وَلا تَهِنُوا): a prohibition. The origin is «توهنوا»; the wāw was dropped because a kasra follows it, and «يوهن» was made to follow it [Translator's note: i.e. the verb with the yāʾ prefix is treated by analogy, «يَهِن»]. (وَأَنْتُمُ الْأَعْلَوْنَ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); the wāw was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, because the fatḥa indicates it.

nahhas-irab:140-140.t:
(إِنْ يَمْسَسْكُمْ قَرْحٌ): the Kufans read قَرْحٌ [Translator's note: presumably «قُرْح», with ḍamma], and Muḥammad al-Yamānī read قَرْحٌ with fatḥa on the rāʾ [«قَرَح»]. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is as though «القَرح» is the pain of wounds and «القُرح» is the wounds themselves. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Akhfash said: they are one and the same. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is like «فَقر» and «فُقر»; as for «القَرَح», it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «قرح يقرح قرحا». (وَتِلْكَ الْأَيَّامُ نُداوِلُها بَيْنَ النَّاسِ): it has been said: this is in war; it is at one time for the believers, so that Allah may give victory to His religion, and at another time for the disbelievers, when the believers disobey, so that Allah may test them and purge their sins.
It has also been said: the meaning of «نداولها بين الناس» is: [We alternate] joy and grief, health and sickness, because of the wretchedness of this world and the superiority of the Hereafter over it. (وَلِيَعْلَمَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): the verb is omitted, i.e. «and so that Allah may know those who believe, He alternated them».
(وَيَتَّخِذَ مِنْكُمْ شُهَداءَ), i.e. so that a people may be killed and thus be witnesses on the Day of Resurrection against people concerning their deeds; and for this reason he is called a «شهيد» (witness/martyr). It has been said: he is called «شهيد» only because he is witnessed (mashhūd lahu) to [be destined for] Paradise.

nahhas-irab:141-141.t: (وَلِيُمَحِّصَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): also conjoined (nasaq). There are three views on its meaning. It has been said: «يمحّص» means tests. Al-Farrāʾ said: i.e. so that Allah may purge the sins of those who believe. The third view is: «يمحّص» means purifies, and this is the best known of them. Al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him, said: one says «محص الحبل يمحص محصا» when its fibres are stripped off it; [and one says] «اللهمّ محّص عنّا ذنوبنا» (O Allah, strip our sins from us), i.e. free us from our punishment. (وَيَمْحَقَ الْكافِرِينَ), i.e. eradicate them.

nahhas-irab:142-143.t: (أَمْ حَسِبْتُمْ أَنْ تَدْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ): «أن» and its ṣila stand in the place of the two objects. (وَلَمَّا يَعْلَمِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ جاهَدُوا مِنْكُمْ), i.e. knowledge of observation (ʿilm shahāda); the meaning is: you have not striven, so that He might know that of you. Sībawayh distinguished between «لم» and «لمّا»: he claimed that «لم يفعل» is the negation of «فعل» (he did), and that «لمّا يفعل» is the negation of «قد فعل» (he has done). (وَيَعْلَمَ الصَّابِرِينَ): the answer to the negation; according to al-Khalīl it is accusative by an implied «أن». The Kufans said: it is accusative by «al-ṣarf» (diversion). It is said to them: «al-ṣarf» must either be something without a cause or with a cause; if with a cause, [that cause is what] makes it accusative, and there is no point in mentioning «al-ṣarf». Al-Ḥasan and Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar read وَلَمَّا يَعْلَمِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ جاهَدُوا مِنْكُمْ وَيَعْلَمَ الصَّابِرِينَ [Translator's note: presumably with the jussive «ويعلمِ»], and this is by conjunction (al-nasaq). Mujāhid read وَلَقَدْ كُنْتُمْ تَمَنَّوْنَ الْمَوْتَ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ تَلْقَوْهُ [Translator's note: the variant itself is not marked in the printed text]. (أَنْ) is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) from «الموت»; and (قَبْلِ) is a «ghāya» (a word cut off from its annexed noun).

nahhas-irab:144-144.t: (وَما مُحَمَّدٌ إِلَّا رَسُولٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ الرُّسُلُ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and the governing effect of «ما» is cancelled. It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he read «قد خلت من قبله رسل» without alif and lām. (أَفَإِنْ ماتَ): a condition. (أَوْ قُتِلَ) is conjoined to it, and the apodosis is (انْقَلَبْتُمْ). All of it is a question, and the alif of interrogation did not enter on «انقلبتم» because it has already entered on the condition, and the condition and its apodosis are like one thing, as are the mubtadaʾ and its khabar: you say «أزيد منطلق؟» (is Zayd leaving?), and you do not say «أزيد أمنطلق».

nahhas-irab:145-145.t: (وَما كانَ لِنَفْسٍ أَنْ تَمُوتَ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ): «أن» is in the position of the ism of «كان». Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is «وما كان لنفس لتموت إلا بإذن الله». Abū Jaʿfar said: «لنفس» is a clarification (tabyīn), and otherwise you would have separated the ṣila from the relative. (كِتاباً مُؤَجَّلًا): a maṣdar (verbal noun). This verse is taken as evidence that every person, killed or not killed, has reached his appointed term, and that creatures must reach their terms, single terms which Allah has written for them, because the meaning of «مؤجّلا» is: until a term.

nahhas-irab:146-146.t: (وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ نَبِيٍّ قاتَلَ): al-Khalīl and Sībawayh said: it is «أيّ» upon which the kāf of comparison has entered, so that the meaning of «كم» (how many) came into the speech; so the pause is on His saying «وكأيّن». Abū Jaʿfar [Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ] and Ibn Kathīr read «وكاإن», which is a lightened form of that, and it is frequent in the speech of the Arabs. Al-Ḥasan, ʿIkrima and Abū Rajāʾ read «رُبّيّون» with ḍamma on the rāʾ. Abū Jaʿfar said: Sībawayh has mentioned the like of this, and we have mentioned the meaning of the verse. Abū al-Sammāl al-ʿAdawī read «فما وهْنوا لما أصابهم» with a sukūn on the hāʾ, and this is according to the dialect of those who say «وهُن». Abū Ḥātim related «وهن يهن» like «ورم يرم». (ما ضَعُفُوا) is also permissible with a sukūn on the ʿayn, by dropping the ḍamma and the kasra because of their heaviness. Al-Kisāʾī related وَما ضَعُفُوا with fatḥa on the ʿayn, and dropping the fatḥa is not permissible because of its lightness.

nahhas-irab:147-147.t: Al-Ḥasan read (وَما كانَ قَوْلَهُمْ) [Translator's note: presumably «قولُهم», in the nominative], making it the ism of «كان»; whoever reads the accusative makes it the khabar of «كان» and makes its ism (أَنْ قالُوا), because it is affirmed (mūjab) [Translator's note: i.e. it comes after «إلا», which affirms it after the negation].

nahhas-irab:150-150.t: Al-Farrāʾ permitted (بَلِ اللَّهُ مَوْلاكُمْ) [in the accusative, «بل اللهَ»] in the sense of «أطيعوا الله مولاكم» (obey Allah, your Protector).

nahhas-irab:151-151.t: (سَنُلْقِي): an imperfect verb; the ḍamma was dropped from the yāʾ because of its heaviness. Abū Jaʿfar, al-Aʿraj and ʿĪsā read سَنُلْقِي فِي قُلُوبِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا الرُّعْبَ [Translator's note: presumably «الرُّعُب» with ḍamma on the ʿayn, not marked in the print], and these are two dialects. (مَثْوَى الظَّالِمِينَ): nominative by «بئس».

nahhas-irab:152-152.t: (وَلَقَدْ صَدَقَكُمُ) may also be [read] with assimilation, and likewise (إِذْ تَحُسُّونَهُمْ). (وَعَصَيْتُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ ما أَراكُمْ ما تُحِبُّونَ مِنْكُمْ مَنْ يُرِيدُ الدُّنْيا): in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), or by the adverbial phrase (al-ṣifa), i.e. among you are those who want booty by their fighting, and among you are those who want the Hereafter by fighting. (ثُمَّ صَرَفَكُمْ عَنْهُمْ): in this verse there is an obscurity in the Arabic, namely that His saying, Majestic and Mighty, (ثُمَّ صَرَفَكُمْ عَنْهُمْ) is not addressed to those who disobeyed; it is addressed only to the believers, because the Prophet ﷺ commanded them to withdraw to the side of the mountain to protect themselves, since they no longer had strength left for fighting. (وَلَقَدْ عَفا عَنْكُمْ) is for the disobedient in particular, who were the archers. This was on the day of Uḥud: victory was at first for the believers, until they killed the standard-bearer of the polytheists, and that is the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: (وَلَقَدْ صَدَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ وَعْدَهُ). Then when the archers disobeyed the Prophet ﷺ and were occupied with the booty, the defeat fell upon them; then Allah pardoned them. A parallel to this [shift of reference] in the pronoun is فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُ عَلَيْهِ [al-Tawba: 40], i.e. upon Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq — he was anxious until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ became clear to him, and then he calmed down — while وَأَيَّدَهُ بِجُنُودٍ لَمْ تَرَوْها [al-Tawba: 40] refers to the Prophet ﷺ.

nahhas-irab:153-153.t: (إِذْ تُصْعِدُونَ وَلا تَلْوُونَ عَلى أَحَدٍ): al-Ḥasan read «ولا تلون» with a single wāw, and we have mentioned its parallel. Abū Yūsuf al-Aʿshā related from Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh, from ʿĀṣim, «ولا تُلوون» with ḍamma on the tāʾ, and it is an anomalous dialect. (فَأَثابَكُمْ غَمًّا بِغَمٍّ لِكَيْلا تَحْزَنُوا عَلى ما فاتَكُمْ): when someone cried out on the day of Uḥud «Muḥammad ﷺ has been killed», their grief over the killing and wounds that had struck them went away because of the gravity of what they had fallen into. It has also been said: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, made them aware of their sin, so they were occupied with that from what had struck them. And it has been said: «فأثابكم» means He requited you by grieving the disbelievers as they grieved you, so that you would not be sad at what struck you and not them.

nahhas-irab:154-154.t:
ثُمَّ أَنْزَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ الْغَمِّ أَمَنَةً نُعاساً يَغْشى طائِفَةً مِنْكُمْ وَطائِفَةٌ قَدْ أَهَمَّتْهُمْ أَنْفُسُهُمْ يَظُنُّونَ بِاللَّهِ غَيْرَ الْحَقِّ ظَنَّ الْجاهِلِيَّةِ يَقُولُونَ هَلْ لَنا مِنَ الْأَمْرِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ قُلْ إِنَّ الْأَمْرَ كُلَّهُ لِلَّهِ يُخْفُونَ فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ ما لا يُبْدُونَ لَكَ يَقُولُونَ لَوْ كانَ لَنا مِنَ الْأَمْرِ شَيْءٌ ما قُتِلْنا هاهُنا قُلْ لَوْ كُنْتُمْ فِي بُيُوتِكُمْ لَبَرَزَ الَّذِينَ كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْقَتْلُ إِلى مَضاجِعِهِمْ وَلِيَبْتَلِيَ اللَّهُ ما فِي صُدُورِكُمْ وَلِيُمَحِّصَ ما فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِذاتِ الصُّدُورِ (154) (ثُمَّ أَنْزَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ الْغَمِّ أَمَنَةً نُعاساً): «أمنة» is accusative by «أنزل», and «نعاس» is a badal (substitute) from it. «أمنة» may also be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), with «نعاسا» [accusative] by «أنزل». «يغشى» [with yāʾ] refers to the drowsiness (al-nuʿās), and «تغشى» [with tāʾ] to the security (al-amana).
(وَطائِفَةٌ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is (قَدْ أَهَمَّتْهُمْ أَنْفُسُهُمْ). The khabar may also be (يَظُنُّونَ بِاللَّهِ غَيْرَ الْحَقِّ), with the wāw in the sense of «إذ» (when) and the clause in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). In Arabic, «وطائفةً» in the accusative is also permissible, by an implied «أهمّت». (ظَنَّ الْجاهِلِيَّةِ): a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. they think a thought like the thought of the Jāhiliyya; the adjective has been put in the place of the noun qualified, and the muḍāf in the place of the muḍāf ilayhi [Translator's note: so in the text; the usual formulation is that the muḍāf ilayhi takes the place of the omitted muḍāf]. (يَقُولُونَ هَلْ لَنا مِنَ الْأَمْرِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ): the first «من» is partitive and the second is redundant (zāʾida). (قُلْ إِنَّ الْأَمْرَ كُلَّهُ لِلَّهِ): the ism of «إنّ», and «كلّه» is tawkīd (emphasis); al-Akhfash said: a badal (substitute). Abū ʿAmr, Ibn Abī Laylā and ʿĪsā read قُلْ إِنَّ الْأَمْرَ كُلَّهُ لِلَّهِ [«كلُّه»], nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with «لله» the khabar and the clause the khabar of «إنّ». (قُلْ لَوْ كُنْتُمْ فِي بُيُوتِكُمْ): the Kufans read «في بِيوتكم» with kasra on the bāʾ, replacing the ḍamma with a kasra because of its adjacency to the yāʾ. (لَبَرَزَ الَّذِينَ كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْقَتْلُ إِلى مَضاجِعِهِمْ): Abū Ḥaywa read لَبَرَزَ [Translator's note: presumably «لَبُرِّزَ», the passive of the doubled form; the variant is not marked in the print]. The meaning is: had you been in your houses, those for whom killing was written in the Preserved Tablet would have gone out to their places of death. It has been said: «كتب» means «فرض» (was prescribed).
(وَلِيَبْتَلِيَ اللَّهُ ما فِي صُدُورِكُمْ): the verb that goes with the lām of kay (purpose) is omitted, and the meaning is: «and so that Allah may test what is in your breasts, He prescribed fighting and war for you and did not give you victory on the day of Uḥud», so as to test your patience and to purge your evil deeds from you.

nahhas-irab:155-155.t: (الَّذِينَ) is the ism of «إنّ», and the khabar (predicate) is (إِنَّمَا اسْتَزَلَّهُمُ الشَّيْطانُ بِبَعْضِ ما كَسَبُوا), i.e. he sought their slipping by reminding them of their sins, so that they disliked standing firm lest they be killed. It has also been said: «ببعض ما كسبوا» means by their running away.

nahhas-irab:156-156.t:
يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَقالُوا لِإِخْوانِهِمْ إِذا ضَرَبُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ أَوْ كانُوا غُزًّى لَوْ كانُوا عِنْدَنا ما ماتُوا وَما قُتِلُوا لِيَجْعَلَ اللَّهُ ذلِكَ حَسْرَةً فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ وَاللَّهُ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ (156) (غُزًّى): the plural of «غاز» (raider), like «صائم» and «صوّم»; one also says «غزّاء», as one says «صوّام»; and one says «غزاة» and «غزيّ», as the poet said: [al-Kāmil] 86-
قل للقوافل والغزيّ إذا غزوا
(Say to the caravans and to the raiders when they go raiding.)
It is related from al-Zuhrī that he read غُزًّى without doubling [«غُزًى»]. (لِيَجْعَلَ اللَّهُ ذلِكَ حَسْرَةً فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ): there are two views on it. One of them is that the meaning is that Allah, Majestic and Mighty, made [a source of anguish] their thinking that, had their brothers stayed with them and not gone out with the Prophet ﷺ, they would not have been killed. The other view is that when they said this, the believers paid no attention to their words, and that was an anguish [for them]. (وَاللَّهُ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ), i.e. He is able to give life to whoever goes out to fight and to cause the death of whoever stays with his family.

nahhas-irab:157-157.t: (وَلَئِنْ قُتِلْتُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أَوْ مُتُّمْ): ʿĪsā said: the people of the Ḥijāz say «مِتّم» and the lower [Najdī] Muḍar say «مُتّم» with ḍamma on the mīm. Abū Jaʿfar said: the view of Sībawayh is that it [«مِتّ»] is anomalous, coming on «متّ يموت», and its like in his view is «فضل يفضل». As for the Kufans, they said: whoever says «مِتّ» says «يمات», like «خفت تخاف», and whoever says «مُتّ» says «يموت»; and this is a good view. The answer to «أو» [i.e. to the oath] is (لَمَغْفِرَةٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرَحْمَةٌ خَيْرٌ مِمَّا يَجْمَعُونَ), and it is construed according to the sense, because the meaning of «ولئن قتلتم في سبيل الله أو متّم» is «He will surely forgive you».

nahhas-irab:158-158.t: (وَلَئِنْ مُتُّمْ أَوْ قُتِلْتُمْ لَإِلَى اللَّهِ تُحْشَرُونَ): He admonished them with this, i.e. do not flee from fighting and from what I have commanded you, but flee from the punishment of Allah, for to Him you will be gathered; no one other than Him has power to harm or benefit you.

nahhas-irab:159-159.t:
(فَبِما رَحْمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ): «ما» is redundant (zāʾida), and (رَحْمَةٍ) is genitive by the bāʾ. «ما» may also be an indefinite noun, genitive by the bāʾ, with «رحمة» a naʿt (adjective) of «ما». «فبما رحمةٌ» is also permissible, i.e. «فبالذي هو رحمة» (by that which is a mercy), i.e. a kindness from Allah, Majestic and Mighty. (لِنْتَ لَهُمْ). [The indefinite «ما»] is as the poet said: [al-Kāmil] 87-
فكفى بنا فضلا على من غيرنا
(It suffices us as a merit over someone other than us.)
— and «غيرُ» [in the nominative] as well. (وَلَوْ كُنْتَ فَظًّا): on the pattern faʿl; the origin is «فظظ». (فَاعْفُ عَنْهُمْ وَاسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ وَشاوِرْهُمْ فِي الْأَمْرِ): the maṣdar (verbal noun) is «مشاورة» and «شوار»; as for «مشورة» and «شورى», they are from the triliteral. (فَإِذا عَزَمْتَ فَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ): Jābir ibn Zayd Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ and Abū Nahīk read فَإِذا عَزَمْتَ [Translator's note: presumably «عَزَمْتُ», first person; the variant is not marked in the print], i.e. then rely on Allah, i.e. do not rely on your equipment, but strengthen yourself through Allah. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُتَوَكِّلِينَ).

nahhas-irab:160-160.t: (إِنْ يَنْصُرْكُمُ اللَّهُ فَلا غالِبَ لَكُمْ): a condition, and the apodosis is in the fāʾ and what follows it; and likewise (وَإِنْ يَخْذُلْكُمْ فَمَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يَنْصُرُكُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ). (وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ), i.e. let them trust in Allah and be content with everything He does. This is the meaning of tawakkul (reliance).

nahhas-irab:161-161.t: (وَما كانَ لِنَبِيٍّ أَنْ يَغُلَّ): we have already mentioned it, and we mentioned the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās يَغُلَّ [Translator's note: presumably «يُغَلّ», the passive; not marked in the print]. (وَمَنْ يَغْلُلْ): a condition. (يَأْتِ بِما غَلَّ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ): its apodosis, i.e. whoever embezzles [will come] with what he embezzled on the Day of Resurrection, carrying it before the eyes of all witnesses as a punishment for him. In this is an admonition to everyone who commits an act of disobedience while concealing it. The statement is complete. (ثُمَّ تُوَفَّى كُلُّ نَفْسٍ): conjoining a clause to a clause.
