nahhas-irab:163-163.t: (هُمْ دَرَجاتٌ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). «هم» may refer to those who followed the pleasure of Allah and entered Paradise, i.e. they are of different ranks; and «هم» may refer both to those who followed the pleasure of Allah and to those who incurred His wrath, the meaning being: each one of them has his share of his deeds.

nahhas-irab:164-164.t: (إِذْ): an adverbial (ẓarf). Concerning the meaning of the favour (al-minna) in it there are several views. Among them: that the meaning of «من أنفسهم» (from among themselves) is that he is a human being like them, so when he manifested the proofs while being a human being like them, it was known that that was from Allah, Majestic and Mighty. It has been said: «من أنفسهم» means one of them, so they were honoured by him, and that was the favour. And it has been said: «من أنفسهم» means they know him for truthfulness and trustworthiness. As for the view of whoever says that its meaning is «from the Arabs», so that they would be more apt to believe him since he was not from others — that is wrong, because they would have had no argument in that had he been from others, just as others have no argument in that. (يَتْلُوا عَلَيْهِمْ) is in the position of the accusative, a naʿt (adjective) of «رسول».

nahhas-irab:165-165.t: (أَوَلَمَّا أَصابَتْكُمْ مُصِيبَةٌ قَدْ أَصَبْتُمْ مِثْلَيْها): the calamity which struck them on the day of Uḥud — they had inflicted twice its like on the day of Badr. It has also been said: they had inflicted twice its like on the day of Badr and the day of Uḥud together.

nahhas-irab:166-166.t: (فَبِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ): it has been said: by His knowledge; but «al-idhn» is not known in this [sense] other than as permission; rather, «فبإذن الله» means: by His leaving [the field] open between you and them. (وَلِيَعْلَمَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ).

nahhas-irab:167-167.t: (وَلِيَعْلَمَ الَّذِينَ نافَقُوا): the verb is omitted, i.e. He left [the field] open between you and them. The hypocrites were ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy and his companions; they withdrew in flight on the day of Uḥud to Medina, so when (وَقِيلَ لَهُمْ تَعالَوْا قاتِلُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أَوِ ادْفَعُوا قالُوا لَوْ نَعْلَمُ قِتالًا لَاتَّبَعْناكُمْ), Allah, Majestic and Mighty, exposed them as liars, and said: قِيلَ لَهُمْ تَعالَوْا قاتِلُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أَوِ ادْفَعُوا قالُوا لَوْ نَعْلَمُ قِتالًا لَاتَّبَعْناكُمْ.

nahhas-irab:168-168.t: (الَّذِينَ قالُوا لِإِخْوانِهِمْ) is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of «الذين نافقوا», or by «أعني» (I mean); it may also be nominative with an implied mubtadaʾ (subject). (قُلْ فَادْرَؤُا عَنْ أَنْفُسِكُمُ الْمَوْتَ), i.e. just as you are unable to repel death from yourselves, so you are unable to prevent from being killed one whom Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has written to be killed.

nahhas-irab:169-169.t: (وَلا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ قُتِلُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أَمْواتاً): two objects. (بَلْ أَحْياءٌ), i.e. «بل هم أحياء» (rather, they are alive).

nahhas-irab:1-3.t: الم اللَّهُ: al-Ḥasan, ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd, ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd and Abū Jaʿfar al-Ruʾāsī read «الم أَللهُ» with the alif cut [i.e. pronouncing the hamza]. Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: «الم ِاللهُ» with kasra on the mīm is permitted, because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. [Translator's note: the source prints both variants with the standard vowelling; the forms given follow the descriptions.] Abū Jaʿfar said: the first reading is the reading of the generality [of readers], and the early grammarians have discussed it. Sībawayh's view is that the mīm was given fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and they chose fatḥa for it so as not to combine a kasra and a yāʾ with a kasra before it. Sībawayh said: if you intended continuous recitation you would say «الم اللهُ», giving the mīm fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, as was done with أين and كيف. Al-Kisāʾī said: when the letters of the alphabet are met by the connecting alif and the connecting alif is dropped, you give them the vowel of the alif, so you say «الم الله», «الم اذكروا» and «الم اقتربت». Al-Farrāʾ said: the original is «الم أَلله», as al-Ruʾāsī read; the vowel of the hamza was cast onto the mīm. Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Kaysān said: the alif with the lām is on a par with «قد», and its rule is the rule of the cutting alif, because both are particles that came for a meaning; it was only connected because of frequent use, and for this reason one begins it with fatḥa. Abū Isḥāq said: what al-Akhfash reported, kasra on the mīm, is a mistake that is not permitted, and the Arabs do not say it because of its heaviness. الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, read «القيّام», and Khārija said: in the Muṣḥaf of ʿAbd Allāh it is «الحيّ القيّم». Abū Jaʿfar said: القيّوم is on the pattern فَيْعُول, its original being قيووم, then assimilation occurred; القيّام is فَيْعال, its original being القيوام, then it was assimilated; and قيّم is فَيْعِل according to the Basrans, its original being قيوم, then it was assimilated. Al-Farrāʾ claimed it is فَعِيل. Ibn Kaysān said: had it been as he said, it would not have been made defective, just as سويق and its like are not made defective. The name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is نَزَّلَ عَلَيْكَ الْكِتابَ, and الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ is a naʿt (adjective). Or, if you wish, the khabar is لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ, then a khabar after a khabar was brought. مُصَدِّقاً: accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial), and according to the Kufans by qaṭʿ (severance). Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned the derivation of التَّوْراةَ وَالْإِنْجِيلَ in the book before this.

nahhas-irab:4-6.t: مِنْ قَبْلُ: [an adverb cut off from annexation and made indeclinable as] a ghāya (limit), and we have mentioned it. هُدىً: in the position of accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial); the case does not show in it because it is maqṣūr (ending in alif). إِنَّ الَّذِينَ: the noun of إنّ; the ṣila (relative clause) is كَفَرُوا بِآياتِ اللَّهِ, and the khabar (predicate) is لَهُمْ عَذابٌ شَدِيدٌ. وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ ذُو انْتِقامٍ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar, and likewise هُوَ الَّذِي يُصَوِّرُكُمْ. Al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Faḍl narrated from Abū ʿAmr «هو الذي يصوّرْكم» [Translator's note: the source prints the narrated form with the standard vowelling; the variant intended is presumably with sukūn on the rāʾ].

nahhas-irab:7-7.t:
This whole verse is difficult. We have mentioned it, and we will explain it further, if Allah wills. Abū Jaʿfar said: the best of what has been said about the muḥkamāt (decisive verses) and the mutashābihāt (ambiguous verses) is that the muḥkamāt are what stand by themselves, not needing reference to something else, such as وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُواً أَحَدٌ [al-Ikhlāṣ: 4] and وَإِنِّي لَغَفَّارٌ لِمَنْ تابَ وَآمَنَ [Ṭāhā: 82]; and the mutashābihāt are such as إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعاً [al-Zumar: 53], for which reference is made to His saying وَإِنِّي لَغَفَّارٌ لِمَنْ تابَ [Ṭāhā: 82] and to His saying إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَغْفِرُ أَنْ يُشْرَكَ بِهِ [al-Nisāʾ: 48]. As for «أخر» not being fully declined, it is because it is diverted (maʿdūla) from [the form with] the alif and lām; we have mentioned this. فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ زَيْغٌ: «الذين» is in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is فَيَتَّبِعُونَ ما تَشابَهَ مِنْهُ. One says زاغ يزيغ زيغا when one abandons the right course. ابْتِغاءَ الْفِتْنَةِ: mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. seeking the trial in which there is excess and the corruption of mutual relations; from it is «فلان مفتون بفلانة» (so-and-so is infatuated with such-and-such a woman), i.e. he has gone to excess in loving her. وَما يَعْلَمُ تَأْوِيلَهُ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَالرَّاسِخُونَ: conjoined to Allah, Majestic and Mighty. This is the best of what has been said about it, because Allah, Majestic and Mighty, praised them for being firmly grounded in knowledge, so how would He praise them while they are ignorant? Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned more than this argument. As for the reading narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, «وما يعلم تأويله إلّا الله ويقول الراسخون في العلم», it differs from our Muṣḥaf; and even if it were sound, there would be no proof in it for whoever stops [at الله], [because it would be] "and those firmly grounded in knowledge [know it], and those firmly grounded in knowledge say: we believe in Allah", the pronoun of الراسخين being made overt to clarify the meaning, as Sībawayh recited: [al-Khafīf] 70-
لا أرى الموت يسبق الموت شيء ... نغّص الموت ذا الغنى والفقيرا
(I do not see anything outrunning death; death has spoiled [life] for the rich and the poor alike.)
If someone says: some of its interpretation was difficult for those firmly grounded in knowledge, so that Ibn ʿAbbās said: I do not know what الأوّاه [al-Tawba: 114] is, nor غِسْلِينٍ [al-Ḥāqqa: 36]; this is not binding, because Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah have mercy on him, learned [them] after that and explained what he had held back on. A more decisive answer than this: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, only said وَما يَعْلَمُ تَأْوِيلَهُ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَالرَّاسِخُونَ فِي الْعِلْمِ, and did not say, Majestic and Mighty, "and every firmly grounded one", so that this would be required; so if one of them does not know it, another knows it. Ibn Kaysān said: one also says «الراصخون» with ṣād, a dialect form, because a khāʾ follows it. يَقُولُونَ: in the position of accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) from الراسخين, as the poet said: [Majzūʾ al-Kāmil] 71-
الرّيح تبكي شجوه ... والبرق يلمع في الغمامه
(The wind weeps his grief, and the lightning flashes in the cloud.)
It may also be that الراسخون في العلم is the completion of the speech, and يقولون is resumptive.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t:
رَبَّنا لا تُزِغْ قُلُوبَنا: jussive (majzūm), because its form is the form of the prohibition. «لا تَزِغْ قلوبُنا» is permitted, nominative by its verb, and «لا يَزِغْ قلوبُنا» is permitted, treating the plural as masculine. [Translator's note: the source writes these variants unvowelled; the vowelling follows the descriptions.] وَهَبْ لَنا مِنْ لَدُنْكَ رَحْمَةً: لدن is not declined because it is not fully nominal (ghayr mutamakkin). There are nine dialect forms of it: the dialect of the people of the Hijaz is لَدُن; one also says لدنْ with sukūn on the nūn, and لدنِ with kasra on it. Al-Farrāʾ said: some of the Banū Tamīm say لَدْ; al-ʿAjjāj said: [al-Rajaz] 72-
من لد شولا فإلى إتلائها
(From the time [the she-camel's] milk dried up, until her being followed by her young.)
Al-Kisāʾī reported «لَدُ يا هذا», and Abū Ḥātim reported لَدْ with sukūn on the dāl. Al-Farrāʾ said: Rabīʿa say «من لَدْنِ يا هذا» with sukūn on the dāl and kasra on the nūn; Asad say لُدُنْ with ḍamma on the lām and the dāl and sukūn on the nūn; Abū Ḥātim reported «لُدْن يا هذا» with ḍamma on the lām and sukūn on the dāl. One also says لدى meaning لدن. [Translator's note: the source writes the forms unvowelled; the vowelling given follows the descriptions where these are stated, and only eight forms are actually listed.]

nahhas-irab:9-9.t:
رَبَّنا إِنَّكَ جامِعُ النَّاسِ: «جامعٌ الناسَ» with tanwīn and the accusative is permitted, and it is the original; the tanwīn was dropped for lightness. «جامعُ الناسَ» without tanwīn and with the accusative is also permitted [Translator's note: the source writes these variants without vowels]. Sībawayh recited:
[al-Mutaqārib] 73-
فألفيته غير مستعتب ... ولا ذاكر الله إلّا قليلا
(I found him not seeking to make amends, nor remembering Allah except a little.)

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَنْ تُغْنِيَ عَنْهُمْ أَمْوالُهُمْ: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read «لن يغني عنهم أموالهم» [with yāʾ], because [words] intervene and it is a non-real feminine. Abū Ḥātim said: with the tāʾ is better, like شَغَلَتْنا أَمْوالُنا [al-Fatḥ: 11]. وَأُولئِكَ هُمْ وَقُودُ النَّارِ: al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid and Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read «وُقود» with ḍamma on the wāw. In Arabic it is permitted, when the wāw has ḍamma, to say أُقود, like أُقِّتَتْ [al-Mursalāt: 11].

nahhas-irab:11-11.t:
We have mentioned the position of the kāf. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the meaning is: the Arabs disbelieved with a disbelief like the disbelief of the people of Pharaoh. Abū Jaʿfar said: it is not permissible for the kāf to be attached (mutaʿalliq) to كفروا, because كفروا is inside the ṣila (relative clause) and كدأب is outside it. Abū Ḥātim said: I heard Yaʿqūb mention «كدأَب» with fatḥa on the hamza, and he said to me when I was a young boy: on what basis is «كدأَب» permitted? I said: I think it is from دئب يدأب دأبا. That was accepted from me, and he marvelled at the excellence of my analysis despite my youth; but I do not know whether that is said or not.
Abū Jaʿfar said: this view is a mistake; دئب is not said at all. One only says دأب يدأب, دؤوبا and دأبا; so the grammarians have reported, among them al-Farrāʾ, who reported it in «Kitāb al-Maṣādir», as the poet said:
[al-Ṭawīl] 74-
كدأبك من أمّ الحويرث قبلها ... وجارتها أمّ الرّباب بمأسل
(As was your habit with Umm al-Ḥuwayrith before her, and her neighbour Umm al-Rabāb, at Maʾsal.)
As for الدأَب, it is permitted, as one says شعْر and شعَر, نهْر and نهَر, because it contains one of the guttural letters.

nahhas-irab:170-170.t:
(فَرِحِينَ): accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); outside the Qur'an its nominative would be permissible, as a naʿt (adjective) of «أحياء».
(وَيَسْتَبْشِرُونَ بِالَّذِينَ لَمْ يَلْحَقُوا بِهِمْ مِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ): it has been said: who have not caught up with them in merit; and it has been said: they are [still] in this world. (أَلَّا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ) is a badal (substitute) from «الذين», and it is a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl); the meaning may also be «بأن لا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون» (that there is no fear upon them, nor will they grieve).

nahhas-irab:172-172.t: (الَّذِينَ اسْتَجابُوا لِلَّهِ وَالرَّسُولِ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is (لِلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا مِنْهُمْ وَاتَّقَوْا أَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ). «الذين» may also be a badal (substitute) from «المؤمنين», or a badal from «الذين لم يلحقوا بهم».

nahhas-irab:173-173.t: (الَّذِينَ قالَ لَهُمُ النَّاسُ) is a badal (substitute) from «الذين» before it. (وَقالُوا حَسْبُنَا اللَّهُ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), i.e. Allah suffices us. One says «أحسبه» when he gave him enough. (وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ): nominative by «نعم», i.e. how excellent a guardian and keeper is Allah, and the helper of whoever helps Him.

nahhas-irab:175-175.t: We have already mentioned (إِنَّما ذلِكُمُ الشَّيْطانُ يُخَوِّفُ أَوْلِياءَهُ).

nahhas-irab:176-176.t: (وَلا يَحْزُنْكَ الَّذِينَ يُسارِعُونَ فِي الْكُفْرِ): this is the more eloquent of the two dialects, and he said «يحزنك» [Translator's note: the other dialect, «يُحزِنك» from «أحزن», is implied; the print does not distinguish the vowelling]. It is said that these were a people who became Muslim and then apostatised out of fear of the polytheists, and the Prophet ﷺ was grieved; so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, revealed (وَلا يَحْزُنْكَ الَّذِينَ يُسارِعُونَ فِي الْكُفْرِ إِنَّهُمْ لَنْ يَضُرُّوا اللَّهَ شَيْئاً), i.e. they will not harm the friends of Allah when they abandon helping them, since Allah, Majestic and Mighty, is their helper.

nahhas-irab:177-177.t: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ اشْتَرَوُا الْكُفْرَ بِالْإِيْمانِ): a figurative usage (majāz): He made the disbelief they took in exchange and the Islam they abandoned like selling and buying.

nahhas-irab:179-179.t:
(ما كانَ اللَّهُ لِيَذَرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلى ما أَنْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ): the lām of negation (lām al-nafy, lām al-juḥūd), with «أن» implied, except that it never appears overtly.
Among the best things said about the verse is that the meaning is: Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in, of the believers being mixed with the hypocrites, until He distinguishes between them by trial and obligation, so that you know the believer from the hypocrite — the bad one being the hypocrite and the good one the believer. It has also been said: the meaning is that Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in of mere profession, until He imposes the obligations upon them. And it has been said: this is addressed to the hypocrites specifically, i.e. Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in, of enmity to the Prophet ﷺ. (وَما كانَ اللَّهُ لِيُطْلِعَكُمْ عَلَى الْغَيْبِ), i.e. He would not identify the hypocrites for you so that you know them, but that becomes apparent through obligation and trial. It has also been said: Allah would not let you know what will come from them. (وَلكِنَّ اللَّهَ يَجْتَبِي مِنْ رُسُلِهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ), and He acquaints him with whatever He wills of that.

nahhas-irab:180-180.t:
The people of Medina and most of the readers read (وَلا يَحْسَبَنَّ) with yāʾ in both places together, and Ḥamza read with tāʾ in both. Abū Ḥātim claimed that it is a solecism (laḥn) that is not permissible, and a group followed him in that. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read أَنَّما نُمْلِي لَهُمْ [Āl ʿImrān: 178] with kasra on «إن» in both places together. Abū Ḥātim said: I heard al-Akhfash mention the kasra of «إن», using it as an argument for the people of qadar (the Qadariyya), because he was one of them, and taking it as fronting and postponing, i.e. «ولا يحسبنّ الذين كفروا إنما نملي لهم ليزدادوا إثما، إنما نملي لهم خير لأنفسهم». He said: and I saw in a codex in the congregational mosque that they had added a letter to it, so that it became «إنّما نملي لهم ليزدادوا إيمانا» (We only grant them respite that they may increase in faith); Yaʿqūb the reader looked at it, recognised the interpolation, and scraped it off.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the implied construction on the reading of Nāfiʿ is that «أنّ» stands in for the two objects. As for the reading of Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ claimed that it is permissible by repetition (al-takrīr), i.e. «ولا تحسبنّ الذين كفروا، لا تحسبنّ إنما نملي لهم». Abū Isḥāq said: «أنّ» is a badal (substitute) from «الذين», i.e. «ولا يحسبن أنما نملي لهم خير لأنفسهم», i.e. [do not think] our granting respite to those who disbelieve to be good for themselves, as the poet said: [al-Ṭawīl] 88-
فما كان قيس هلكه هلك واحد ... ولكنّه بنيان قوم تهدّما
(Qays's death was not the death of a single man; rather it was the edifice of a people that collapsed.)
Abū Jaʿfar said: the reading of Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb with kasra on «إن» in both places together is good, as you say «حسبت عمرا أبوه خارج» (I thought ʿAmr — his father is going out). As for (وَلا يَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ) on the reading of Nāfiʿ, «الذين» is in the position of the nominative and the first object is omitted. Al-Khalīl, Sībawayh, al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning is «البخل هو خيرا لهم» (stinginess — it is good for them); «هو» is redundant (zāʾida): a support (ʿimād) according to the Kufans and a separating pronoun (fāṣila) according to the Basrans. Like this implied [noun] is the saying of the poet: [al-Wāfir] 89-
إذا نهي السّفيه جرى إليه ... وخالف والسفيه إلى خلاف
(When the fool is forbidden, he runs towards it [folly] and disobeys; and the fool tends to contrariness.)
When he said «السفيه» (the fool), it indicated «السفه» (folly) [Translator's note: the printed text has «السفل»], so he implied it; and when He, Majestic and Mighty, said «يبخلون», it indicated «البخل» (stinginess). Its parallel is the saying of the Arabs: «من كذب كان شرا له» (whoever lies, it is bad for him). As for the reading of Ḥamza «ولا تحسبنّ الذين يبخلون», it is very far-fetched, and its justification would be that the implied construction is «ولا تحسبنّ [بخل] الذين يبخلون», like وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ [Yūsuf: 82]. In Arabic «وهو خيرٌ لهم» is permissible, as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). (بَلْ هُوَ شَرٌّ لَهُمْ): a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and likewise (وَلِلَّهِ مِيراثُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ), and likewise (وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ). «البُخل» and «البَخَل» in the language mean that a person withholds the right that is due from him; as for one who withholds what is not due from him, he is not a miser, because he is not blamed for that. The people of the Ḥijāz say «يبخُلون» and «قد بخِلوا», and the rest of the Arabs say «بخُلوا يبخُلون» [Translator's note: the vowelling distinguishing the two dialects is not shown in the print]. Some of the Banū ʿĀmir say «يجدبي», i.e. «يجتبي», replacing the tāʾ with a dāl when a jīm precedes it, and they say «يجدلون», i.e. «يجتلدون».

nahhas-irab:181-181.t: (لَقَدْ سَمِعَ اللَّهُ): if you wish, you may assimilate the dāl into the sīn because of its nearness to it. (قَوْلَ الَّذِينَ قالُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ فَقِيرٌ وَنَحْنُ أَغْنِياءُ): «إن» takes kasra because it is reported speech (ḥikāya), and some Arabs give it a fatḥa. The exegetes said: when Allah, Majestic and Mighty, revealed مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يُقْرِضُ اللَّهَ قَرْضاً حَسَناً [al-Baqara: 245], a group of the Jews said: Allah is poor, borrowing from us. They said this only to mislead their weak ones, not that they believed it, because they were people of scripture; but they disbelieved by this saying, because they intended to make the believers doubt and to give the lie to the Prophet ﷺ, i.e. [He is] poor according to what Muḥammad ﷺ says, because He borrows from us. (سَنَكْتُبُ ما قالُوا): [«ما»] is accusative by «سنكتب». Al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read «سيُكتب ما قالوا», so «ما» here is the deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil); Ḥamza took into account the reading of Ibn Masʿūd «ويقال ذوقوا عذاب الحريق». (وَقَتْلَهُمُ الْأَنْبِياءَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ), i.e. and We will write their killing, i.e. their being pleased with the killing. (وَنَقُولُ ذُوقُوا عَذابَ الْحَرِيقِ), i.e. We will rebuke them with this.

nahhas-irab:182-182.t: (ذلِكَ بِما قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ): the ḍamma was dropped from the yāʾ because of its heaviness.

nahhas-irab:183-183.t: (الَّذِينَ قالُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَهِدَ إِلَيْنا) is in the position of the genitive, as a badal (substitute) from «الذين» in His saying لَقَدْ سَمِعَ اللَّهُ قَوْلَ الَّذِينَ قالُوا [verse 181]. (أَلَّا نُؤْمِنَ) is in the position of the accusative. Al-Mulhim, the companion of al-Akhfash, said: whoever assimilates with nasalisation (ghunna) writes «أن لا» separately, and whoever assimilates without nasalisation writes «ألّا» joined. It has also been said: rather, it is written separately because it is «أن» upon which «لا» has entered. And it has been said: whoever makes the verb accusative writes it joined, and whoever makes it nominative writes it separately. (حَتَّى يَأْتِيَنا): accusative by «حتى». ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read (بِقُرْبانٍ) with ḍamma on the rāʾ. If you pluralise «قربان» you say «قرابين» and «قرابنة». (قُلْ قَدْ جاءَكُمْ رُسُلٌ مِنْ قَبْلِي): on the basis of treating the plural as masculine, i.e. [they] came to your forefathers, and when they came to their forefathers, they came to them. (بِالْبَيِّناتِ): with the miraculous signs. (وَبِالَّذِي قُلْتُمْ): with the offering. (فَلِمَ قَتَلْتُمُوهُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ), i.e. if you are truthful that Allah, Majestic and Mighty, made a covenant with you that you should not believe until you are brought an offering which the fire consumes.

nahhas-irab:184-184.t: (فَإِنْ كَذَّبُوكَ): a condition. (فَقَدْ كُذِّبَ رُسُلٌ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ): its apodosis. This is a consolation for him ﷺ.

nahhas-irab:185-185.t: (كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). (وَإِنَّما تُوَفَّوْنَ أُجُورَكُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ): «ما» is restrictive (kāffa), and it cannot have the meaning of «الذي», for if that were so you would have said «أجورُكم», making it nominative as the khabar of «إن», and you would have separated the ṣila from the relative. (وَمَا الْحَياةُ الدُّنْيا إِلَّا مَتاعُ الْغُرُورِ): a mubtadaʾ and khabar, i.e. it is perishing, so it is like that which deludes and deceives.

nahhas-irab:186-186.t: (لَتُبْلَوُنَّ فِي أَمْوالِكُمْ وَأَنْفُسِكُمْ وَلَتَسْمَعُنَّ): the lām of the oath. If it is asked: why is the wāw retained in «لتبلونّ» and dropped from «لتسمعنّ»? The answer is that the wāw in «لتبلونّ» has a fatḥa before it, so it was given a vowel because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and dropping it was not permissible because there is nothing before it to indicate it; and it was dropped in «ولتسمعنّ» because before it there is something that indicates it. It is not permissible to give the wāw in «لتبلونّ» a hamza, because its vowel is incidental.

nahhas-irab:187-187.t: (وَإِذْ أَخَذَ اللَّهُ مِيثاقَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ لَتُبَيِّنُنَّهُ): as a report of the address (in the second person). Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim read with yāʾ, because they are absent. The hāʾ is a pronoun referring to the People of the Book [Translator's note: so in the text; in context the hāʾ refers to the Book]; and it has been said: to the Prophet ﷺ, i.e. to his affair.

nahhas-irab:188-188.t: (لا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ يَفْرَحُونَ بِما أَتَوْا): al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī al-Juʿfī related from al-Aʿmash «بما آتوا», i.e. [what] they gave. It has been said: the Jews are meant by this; and in the reading of Ubayy it is «بما فعلوا». Ibn Zayd said: they are the hypocrites; they used to say to the Prophet ﷺ: we will go out and fight with you; then they would stay behind and make excuses, and rejoice at what they had done, because they considered that their ruse had succeeded. (فَلا تَحْسَبَنَّهُمْ بِمَفازَةٍ مِنَ الْعَذابِ): He repeated «تحسبنّ» because of the length of the speech, so that it would be known that the first is meant, as you say: «لا تحسب زيدا إذا جاءك وكلّمك لا تحسبه مناصحا» (do not think Zayd, when he comes to you and speaks to you — do not think him sincere).

nahhas-irab:189-189.t: (وَلِلَّهِ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and likewise (وَاللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ).

nahhas-irab:190-190.t: (إِنَّ فِي خَلْقِ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاخْتِلافِ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهارِ لَآياتٍ): in the position of the accusative, as the ism of «إن». (لِأُولِي): genitive by the lām, and the wāw was added in it [in writing] to distinguish it from «إلى». (الْأَلْبابِ): genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). Sībawayh related from Yūnus «قد لبُبت» (you have become intelligent), and nothing else is known [with this pattern] among the doubled verbs.

nahhas-irab:191-191.t:
(الَّذِينَ يَذْكُرُونَ اللَّهَ) is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of «أولي الألباب». (قِياماً وَقُعُوداً): accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَعَلى جُنُوبِهِمْ) is in the position of a ḥāl, i.e. lying down. (وَيَتَفَكَّرُونَ فِي خَلْقِ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ), i.e. so that that may increase their insight. «ويتفكّرون» may be conjoined to the ḥāl, or to «يذكرون», or cut off (resumptive). (رَبَّنا ما خَلَقْتَ هذا باطِلًا), i.e. You did not create it for the sake of falsehood, i.e. You created it as an indication of You. The implied construction is: [they say]: «باطلا» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). (سُبْحانَكَ), i.e. [we declare] You free of having created this in vain. ʿAbd al-Salām ibn Aḥmad ibn Sahl narrated to us: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Muḥarrar narrated to us: Abū Usāma narrated to us: al-Thawrī narrated to us, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mawhab, from Mūsā ibn Ṭalḥa, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about the meaning of «سبحان الله», and he said:
«Declaring Allah free of evil». (سُبْحانَكَ) is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and it has been annexed on the basis that it is indefinite.

nahhas-irab:193-193.t:
(رَبَّنا): an annexed vocative (munādā muḍāf). (أَنْ آمِنُوا بِرَبِّكُمْ) is in the position of the accusative, i.e. «بأن آمنوا». (وَتَوَفَّنا مَعَ الْأَبْرارِ): the meaning is «and take us as righteous ones with the righteous». Like this entire ellipsis is the poet's saying: [al-Wāfir] 90-
كأنّك من جمال بني أقيش ... يقعقع خلف رجليه بشنّ
(As though you were [a camel] of the camels of the Banū Uqaysh, behind whose legs a dry waterskin is rattled.)
The singular of «الأبرار» is «بارّ», as one says «صاحب» and «أصحاب»; and its singular may also be «برّ», like «كتف» and «أكتاف».

nahhas-irab:194-194.t: (رَبَّنا وَآتِنا ما وَعَدْتَنا عَلى رُسُلِكَ), i.e. on the tongues of Your messengers, like وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ [Yūsuf: 82].

nahhas-irab:195-195.t: (فَاسْتَجابَ لَهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ أَنِّي), i.e. «بأنّي». ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read فَاسْتَجابَ لَهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ أَنِّي with kasra on the hamza [«إنّي»], i.e. and He said: «إني». (بَعْضُكُمْ مِنْ بَعْضٍ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), i.e. your religion is one. (فَالَّذِينَ هاجَرُوا): a mubtadaʾ. (وَأُخْرِجُوا مِنْ دِيارِهِمْ), i.e. in obedience to Allah, Majestic and Mighty. (وَقُتِلُوا) [Translator's note: so printed; the gloss shows «وَقاتَلُوا» is meant], i.e. they fought My enemies. (وَقُتِلُوا), i.e. in My way. Ibn Kathīr and Ibn ʿĀmir read وَقاتَلُوا وَقُتِلُوا [«وقُتِّلوا»], for multiplicity. Al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read «وقُتِلوا وقاتَلوا», because the wāw does not indicate that the second comes after the first. Hārūn the reader said: Yazīd ibn Ḥāzim narrated to me from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, may Allah's mercy be upon him, that he read «وقَتَلوا وقُتِلوا», unstressed, without alif. (لَأُكَفِّرَنَّ عَنْهُمْ سَيِّئاتِهِمْ), i.e. I shall surely cover them for them in the Hereafter, and not rebuke them with them nor punish them for them. (ثَواباً مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ): an emphatic maṣdar (verbal noun) according to the Basrans. Al-Kisāʾī said: it is accusative by «al-qaṭʿ» (severance). Al-Farrāʾ said: it is explicative (mufassir, i.e. tamyīz).

nahhas-irab:196-196.t: (لا يَغُرَّنَّكَ تَقَلُّبُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فِي الْبِلادِ): a prohibition emphasised with the heavy nūn. Ibn Abī Isḥāq and Yaʿqūb read لا يَغُرَّنَّكَ with a light nūn [«لا يغرَّنْك»].

nahhas-irab:197-197.t: (مَتاعٌ قَلِيلٌ), i.e. «ذلك متاع قليل» (that is a small enjoyment), i.e. a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); and likewise (مَأْواهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ). The plural [of «مأوى»] is «مآو».

nahhas-irab:198-198.t: (لكِنِ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا رَبَّهُمْ) is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ read لكِنِ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا with a doubled nūn [«لكنَّ»]. (نُزُلًا مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ) is like «ثوابا» according to the Basrans; al-Kisāʾī said: it may be a maṣdar (verbal noun); and al-Farrāʾ said: it is explicative (mufassir). Al-Ḥasan read «نزْلا» with a sukūn on the zāy, which is the dialect of Tamīm, while the people of the Ḥijāz and the Banū Asad make it heavy (with ḍamma).

nahhas-irab:199-199.t: (وَإِنَّ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتابِ لَمَنْ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ): the ism of «إنّ», and the lām is for emphasis (tawkīd). Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: «وما أنزل إليكم» is the Qur'an, and «وما أنزل إليهم» is the Torah and the Gospel. Al-Ḥasan said: it was revealed about the Negus (al-Najāshī). (خاشِعِينَ لِلَّهِ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in «يؤمن». Al-Kisāʾī said: it may be «qaṭʿ» (severance) from «من», because it is definite, and it may be «qaṭʿ» from «وما أنزل إليهم». Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: (خاشِعِينَ) means humble.

nahhas-irab:200-200.t: (يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اصْبِرُوا): an imperative, and for that reason the nūn has been dropped from it. (وَصابِرُوا وَرابِطُوا) are conjoined to it, and likewise (وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ), i.e. let not your sole concern be jihād only; fear Allah in all your affairs. (لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ), i.e. so that you may be in hope of success (al-falāḥ). Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: «الفلاح» is everlastingness.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: قَدْ كانَ لَكُمْ آيَةٌ فِي فِئَتَيْنِ الْتَقَتا فِئَةٌ تُقاتِلُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: meaning "one of them is a party". Al-Ḥasan and Mujāhid read «فئةٍ تقاتل في سبيل الله وأخرى كافرةٍ» in the genitive, as a badal (substitute). [Translator's note: the source prints the reading with the standard vowelling; the genitive is stated in the text.] Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā said: the accusative is permitted as ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "they met, being different". Abū Isḥāq said: the accusative has the meaning of «أعني» (I mean). «ترونهم مّثليهم»: accusative as ḥāl; and whoever reads «تُرَونهم», the accusative for him is as the predicate of ترى. [Translator's note: the source writes both forms identically; the contrast intended is between ترَونهم / يرَونهم (seeing with the eye, so مثليهم is ḥāl) and the passive تُرَونهم (thinking, so مثليهم is its second object).] We have mentioned the meaning.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t:
زُيِّنَ لِلنَّاسِ حُبُّ الشَّهَواتِ مِنَ النِّساءِ وَالْبَنِينَ وَالْقَناطِيرِ الْمُقَنْطَرَةِ مِنَ الذَّهَبِ وَالْفِضَّةِ وَالْخَيْلِ الْمُسَوَّمَةِ وَالْأَنْعامِ وَالْحَرْثِ ذلِكَ مَتاعُ الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا وَاللَّهُ عِنْدَهُ حُسْنُ الْمَآبِ (14)
زُيِّنَ لِلنَّاسِ حُبُّ الشَّهَواتِ: [حبّ] is the noun whose agent is not named [i.e. the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)]. The hāʾ in الشهوات was given a vowel to distinguish between the noun and the adjective, and making it quiescent is permitted because a wāw follows it. Ibn Kaysān said: some said الْقَناطِيرِ الْمُقَنْطَرَةِ cannot be fewer than nine, because its meaning is "gathered together", and three is قناطير, so when you gather them it becomes like your saying "three threes". الذَّهَبِ is feminine; one says «هي الذهب الحسنة» (it is fine gold), and its plural is ذهاب and ذهوب; it may also be the plural of ذهبة. The plural of فضة is فضض. الخيل is feminine. Ibn Kaysān said: I was told from Abū ʿUbayda that he said: the singular of الخيل is خائل, like طائر and طير; it was called خائل because it struts (يختال) in its gait. Ibn Kaysān said: when you say نَعَم it applies only to camels, and when you say أنعام it applies to camels and everything that grazes. It is not permitted to assimilate the thāʾ of «الحرث» into the dhāl of «ذلك», as was done in يَلْهَثْ ذلِكَ [al-Aʿrāf: 176], because the rāʾ of الحرث is quiescent, so if you assimilated, two quiescent letters would meet.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: قُلْ أَأُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِخَيْرٍ مِنْ ذلِكُمْ، لِلَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي: nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) or by the ṣifa [i.e. the prepositional phrase]. Abū Ḥātim said: «جناتٍ» in the genitive is permitted, as a badal (substitute) of خير; I heard Yaʿqūb and others mention that, and «بشرٍّ من ذلكم النارِ» [al-Ḥajj: 72] in the genitive is permitted. Ibn Kaysān said: «جنّات» is permitted in the genitive as a badal, and in the accusative by repeating the verb; and للذين is then attached (mutaʿalliq) to His saying أَأُنَبِّئُكُمْ according to al-Farrāʾ's view, and is an explication according to al-Akhfash's view, i.e. inoperative (mulghāh). وَأَزْواجٌ مُطَهَّرَةٌ: conjoined to جنات.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: [Translator's note: the source begins this entry with «قال», with nothing following it.] الَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ: in the position of genitive (majrūr), i.e. "for those who are God-fearing in the sight of their Lord, those who say". If you wish, it is nominative, i.e. "they are those who"; and accusative as praise, i.e. "I mean those who".

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: الصَّابِرِينَ: a badal (substitute) of الذين if that is accusative or genitive; if it is nominative, الصابرين means "I mean the patient". وَالصَّادِقِينَ وَالْقانِتِينَ وَالْمُنْفِقِينَ وَالْمُسْتَغْفِرِينَ: all conjoined. بِالْأَسْحارِ: its singular is سحر. You say «سِير به سحرَ يا فتى» (he was taken on a journey at dawn, young man); it is not fully declined because it is diverted from [the form with] the alif and lām and it is definite. It is not permitted to put it in the nominative when it is definite, because adverbs are put in the nominative here only figuratively, so when a cause [of non-declension] occurs in them they are left in their category, accusative. If you make it indefinite, the nominative is permitted in it, and it is declined. Abū Isḥāq said: السحر is from when the night turns away until the second dawn rises.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: شَهِدَ اللَّهُ أَنَّهُ لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ: we have mentioned readings in it and explained their parsing. As for the reading of Abū al-Muhallab «شهداءَ لله», it is accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial); and it is narrated from him «شهداءُ لله», i.e. "they are witnesses for Allah"; and it is narrated from him «شهداءَ الله», and it is narrated from him «شهداءُ الله». [Translator's note: the source writes these four narrations without distinguishing vowels; the vowelling given follows the parsing stated.] قائِماً بِالْقِسْطِ: accusative as an emphatic ḥāl, and according to the Kufans by qaṭʿ (severance). In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is «القائمُ بالقسط», as a naʿt (adjective), and in his reading [Translator's note: the source breaks off here].

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: إِنَّ الدِّينَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الْإِسْلامُ: this is with kasra on «إنّ» and nothing else. Al-Akhfash said: the meaning is: "those who were given the Book did not differ, out of rivalry among themselves, except after knowledge had come to them". Abū Isḥāq said: what is better in my view is that «بغيا» be accusative by what «وما اختلف الذين أوتوا الكتاب» indicates, i.e. "they differed out of rivalry among themselves". وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِآياتِ اللَّهِ: a condition, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسابِ. «يكفرُ» in the nominative is permitted, by making «من» mean الذي (the one who).

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَنِ: the yāʾ was dropped in the written text because the kasra indicates it, and the nūn is a compensation. وَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا: a condition, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is فَإِنَّما عَلَيْكَ الْبَلاغُ. وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِالْعِبادِ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَكْفُرُونَ بِآياتِ اللَّهِ: «الذين» is the noun of إنّ, and the khabar (predicate) is فَبَشِّرْهُمْ بِعَذابٍ أَلِيمٍ. If it is asked: how did the fāʾ enter the khabar of «إنّ», when «إن زيدا فمنطلق» is not permitted? The answer is that when «الذي» is the noun of «إنّ» and there is a verb in its ṣila (relative clause), the speech has the sense of a conditional, so the entry of the fāʾ is permitted. This is not permitted with ليت, لعلّ and كأنّ, because «إنّ» is [only] emphasis. وَيَقْتُلُونَ النَّبِيِّينَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ وَيَقْتُلُونَ الَّذِينَ يَأْمُرُونَ بِالْقِسْطِ مِنَ النَّاسِ: Ḥamza read «ويقاتلون الذين يأمرون بالقسط», and this is a very far-fetched aspect, because parts of the speech are conjoined to each other and the sequence is one, and the exegesis indicates «يقتلون». Abū al-ʿĀliya said: there were people of the Children of Israel to whom the prophets came calling them to Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and they killed them; then people of the believers rose up after them and commanded them to Islam, and they killed them; about them this verse was revealed: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَكْفُرُونَ بِآياتِ اللَّهِ to its end. Shuʿba narrated from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿUbayda, from ʿAbd Allāh, who said: the Children of Israel used to kill seventy prophets in a day, then a market would be held with their killing at the end of the day.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: Abū al-Sammāl al-ʿAdawī read «أولئك الذين حبَطت أعمالهم» [with fatḥa on the bāʾ], and it is an anomalous dialect form. [Translator's note: the source writes the word unvowelled; the variant attributed to Abū al-Sammāl is حبَطت against the standard حبِطت.]

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قالُوا: «ذلك» is in the position of nominative with an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "their affair is that".

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: Al-Kisāʾī said: لِيَوْمٍ لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ, i.e. "on a day". The Basrans said: the meaning is "for the reckoning of a day", and the lām is in its [proper] place. Outside the Quran «وأُفّيت» [for وَوُفِّيَتْ] is permitted, like أُقِّتَتْ [al-Mursalāt: 11].

nahhas-irab:26-26.t:
قُلِ اللَّهُمَّ مالِكَ الْمُلْكِ: al-Farrāʾ, in what he holds, takes the view that the original of اللَّهُمَّ is «يا الله أمّنا منك بخير» (O Allah, bring us good from You); when it became frequent and blended together they dropped part of it, and the ḍamma on the hāʾ is the ḍamma that was in أمّنا, which moved when [the rest] was dropped. Abū Jaʿfar said: according to the Basrans this is among the gravest of errors, so much so that some of them said: this is heresy (ilḥād) concerning the name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Abū Jaʿfar said: the [correct] view on this is what al-Khalīl and Sībawayh said: the original is «يا الله», then they brought two letters as a compensation for two letters, namely the two mīms in compensation for «يا». The proof of this is that none of the eloquent says «يا اللهمّ», because they do not combine a thing and its compensation. The ḍamma on اللهمّ, according to the two of them, is the ḍamma of the nominative one addressed (munādā). As for al-Farrāʾ's saying that the original is «يا الله أمّنا»: if it were so, it would have to be said أؤمم, and that it be assimilated so that it takes ḍamma or kasra, and it would have to be a connecting alif with no status, and it would have to be said «يا اللهمّ»; moreover, how would the meaning be sound in saying "O Allah, bring us good from You"?
مالِكَ الْمُلْكِ تُؤْتِي الْمُلْكَ مَنْ تَشاءُ: and this, no one puts it forward before his supplication. [Translator's note: so in the source; the sentence appears to be connected with the preceding objection to al-Farrāʾ.] مالِكَ الْمُلْكِ is accusative according to Sībawayh as a second vocative, and according to him it may not be an adjective of «اللهمّ» because of the mīm. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd and Ibrāhīm ibn al-Sarī [al-Zajjāj] disagreed with him on this and said: it may be an adjective, just as it is an adjective when you bring يا. تُؤْتِي الْمُلْكَ مَنْ تَشاءُ: Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq narrated from Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr that the delegation of Najrān came to the Prophet ﷺ, and he recited to them Sūrat Āl ʿImrān and explained it to them from its beginning to the head of the eightieth [verse], and he said: «تؤتي الملك من تشاء» is "the kingship of prophethood". Ibn Isḥāq said: they were Christians, so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, made known their obstinacy and their disbelief, and that Jesus ﷺ, even though Allah, Majestic and Mighty, had given him signs indicating his prophethood, such as reviving the dead and other things, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, alone possesses these things, by His saying:

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: So had Jesus been a god, this would have been in his hands; in that there was a lesson and a clear sign. Then Allah, Majestic and Mighty, warned the believers and commanded them not to take them as allies, and He said:

nahhas-irab:28-28.t:
لا يَتَّخِذِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الْكافِرِينَ أَوْلِياءَ مِنْ دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذلِكَ فَلَيْسَ مِنَ اللَّهِ فِي شَيْءٍ إِلاَّ أَنْ تَتَّقُوا مِنْهُمْ تُقاةً وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ اللَّهُ نَفْسَهُ وَإِلَى اللَّهِ الْمَصِيرُ (28)
لا يَتَّخِذِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الْكافِرِينَ: jussive (majzūm) «على التي» [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently a corruption of «على النهي», i.e. as a prohibition], and the dhāl was given kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Al-Kisāʾī said: «لا يتّخذُ المؤمنون» in the nominative is permitted, as a statement, as one says «ينبغي أن تفعل ذلك» (you ought to do that).
وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذلِكَ فَلَيْسَ مِنَ اللَّهِ فِي شَيْءٍ: a condition and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), i.e. "he is not among the allies of Allah", like وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ [Yūsuf: 82]. إِلَّا أَنْ تَتَّقُوا مِنْهُمْ تُقاةً: [تقاة] is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and likewise تقيّة; the original [first radical] is wāw. وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ اللَّهُ نَفْسَهُ: Abū Isḥāq said: i.e. "and Allah warns you of Him(self)" (إيّاه), then they dispensed with that by this, and it became the usage. He said: as for تَعْلَمُ ما فِي نَفْسِي وَلا أَعْلَمُ ما فِي نَفْسِكَ [al-Māʾida: 116], its meaning is "You know what is with me and what is in my reality, and I do not know what is with You nor what is in Your reality". Others said: وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ اللَّهُ نَفْسَهُ, i.e. His punishment, like وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ; and He said تَعْلَمُ ما فِي نَفْسِي, i.e. what is hidden in me, so the soul was put in the place of what is concealed, because it is in it; and وَلا أَعْلَمُ ما فِي نَفْسِكَ is by way of pairing (izdiwāj).

nahhas-irab:30-30.t:
يَوْمَ تَجِدُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ما عَمِلَتْ مِنْ خَيْرٍ مُحْضَراً: يَوْمَ is accusative with the implied form «ويحذّركم الله نفسه يوم تجد كلّ نفس ما عملت من خير محضرا» (Allah warns you of Himself on the day every soul finds the good it did presented); the implied form may also be «وإلى الله المصير يوم تجد كل نفس» (to Allah is the return on the day every soul finds). ما عَمِلَتْ: an object. مُحْضَراً: ḥāl (circumstantial). وَما عَمِلَتْ مِنْ سُوءٍ: conjoined to the first «ما». Had «ما» been cut off from the first, as a condition with a clause conjoined to a clause, only the jussive «تودّ» would be permitted; we know of no one who read it so, though it is permitted in grammar.
أَمَداً: the noun of أنّ. بَيْنَها: an adverb (ẓarf). بَعِيداً: its naʿt (adjective). وَاللَّهُ رَؤُفٌ بِالْعِبادِ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:31-31.t:
قُلْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ: a condition. تُحِبُّونَ: the khabar (predicate) of كنتم. فَاتَّبِعُونِي: a command, and the fāʾ with what follows it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the condition. يُحْبِبْكُمُ اللَّهُ: the answer to the command, and it has the sense of a conditional. Love from Allah, Majestic and Mighty, is praise and reward. It is narrated that the Muslims said: O Messenger of Allah, we do love our Lord; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed قُلْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تُحِبُّونَ اللَّهَ فَاتَّبِعُونِي يُحْبِبْكُمُ اللَّهُ. And from him ﷺ: «من أراد أن يحبّه الله فعليه بصدق الحديث وأداء الأمانة وأن لا يؤذي جاره» ("Whoever wants Allah to love him, let him keep to truthful speech, fulfilling trusts, and not harming his neighbour"). Abū Rajāʾ al-ʿUṭāridī read «فاتّبعوني يَحْببكم الله» with fatḥa on the yāʾ. Al-Kisāʾī said: one says يَحِبّ, تَحِبّ and أَحِبّ, and يِحِبّ with kasra on the yāʾ, تِحِبّ, نِحِبّ and إِحِبّ. He said: this is the dialect of some of Qays, meaning the kasra; and he said: the fatḥa is the dialect of Tamīm, Asad and Qays, and it follows the dialect of whoever said حَبّ, which is a dialect that has died. [Translator's note: the source writes these forms unvowelled; the vowelling given follows the descriptions.] Al-Akhfash said: حببت has not been heard. Al-Farrāʾ said: حببت has not been heard except in a verse that al-Kisāʾī recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 75-
وأقسم لولا تمره ما حببته ... ولا كان أدنى من عبيد ومشرق
(I swear, were it not for his dates I would not have loved him, nor would he have been closer [to me] than ʿUbayd and Mushriq.)
Abū Jaʿfar said: according to the Basrans, kasra on the yāʾ of يحب is not permitted, because of the heaviness of kasra on the yāʾ; as for fatḥa on it, it is known, as محبوب indicates. وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ: conjoined to يحببكم. Maḥbūb narrated from Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ that he assimilated the rāʾ of «يغفر» into the lām of «لكم». Abū Jaʿfar said: al-Khalīl and Sībawayh do not permit assimilating the rāʾ into the lām, lest the trill (takrīr) be lost; and Abū ʿAmr is too eminent to err in the like of this; perhaps he used to make the vowel inaudible, as he does in many things.

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا: a condition, except that it is a past verb that is not declined; the implied form is "if they turn away [persisting] in their disbelief", and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُحِبُّ الْكافِرِينَ.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: إِنَّ اللَّهَ اصْطَفى آدَمَ وَنُوحاً: al-Farrāʾ said: i.e. "Allah chose their religion". Abū Jaʿfar said: this implied form is not needed, because the meaning is "He chose them". It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: Adam was created from the surface (أديم) of the earth. Abū Jaʿfar said: أديم الأرض is its face, so he was named Ādam because he was created from the face of the earth. Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā said: whoever says Ādam was named from أديم الأرض has erred in Arabic, because he would then have to decline it fully, since it would be [on the pattern] فاعل, like طابق. He said: rather, it is derived from one of two things: one is that it is derived from their saying «أدمت فلانا بنفس» (I mixed so-and-so with a soul), i.e. I blended him, so he was called Ādam because he was created from mixtures. He said: and the view in my opinion is that آدم is أفعل from الأدمة (tawny colour) in complexion. Abū Jaʿfar said: what Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā rejected is the view of most grammarians. It is possible for آدم to be أفعل derived from أديم الأرض, and for it to be فاعل as he said, except that we analyse it as أفعل, so it is a diptote. نوح is a foreign name, but it is fully declined because it has three letters; it may also be derived from ناح ينوح. عمران is not fully declined because at its end are an alif and nūn, both additional.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t: ذُرِّيَّةً: al-Akhfash said: it is accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial); the Kufans said: by qaṭʿ (severance); Abū Isḥāq said: it is a badal (substitute). ذرّيّة is derived from الذرّ (tiny ants) because of their great number. There are two analyses of it: it may be فُعْلِيّة, or it may be فُعْلُولة, its original being ذرّورة; they found the doubling heavy, so they replaced the last rāʾ with a yāʾ, then assimilated the wāw into the yāʾ and said ذُرّيّة; one also says ذِرّيّة. بَعْضُها مِنْ بَعْضٍ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:35-35.t: إِذْ قالَتِ امْرَأَتُ عِمْرانَ: Abū ʿUbayda said: «إذ» is redundant (zāʾida). Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: the implied form is "remember when she said". Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is "and He chose the family of ʿImrān when the wife of ʿImrān said". رَبِّ إِنِّي نَذَرْتُ لَكَ ما فِي بَطْنِي مُحَرَّراً: accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial). It has also been said: it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted object, i.e. "I have vowed to You what is in my womb, a boy dedicated", i.e. to serve the house of worship. Abū Jaʿfar said: the first view is more fitting from the standpoint of exegesis, the context of the speech [Translator's note: the source reads «اللام», evidently for «الكلام», as the elaboration below shows] and grammar. As for the exegesis: Abū Ṣāliḥ narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: the wife of ʿImrān conceived after she had grown old, and she vowed what was in her womb as dedicated. ʿImrān said to her: what have you done, woe to you! She gave birth to a female, and her Lord accepted her with a goodly acceptance; only boys used to be dedicated. The rabbis cast lots over her with the pens with which they wrote the revelation, and Zakariyyā took charge of her and found her a wet-nurse. When she grew up he made her a sanctuary (miḥrāb) which could be reached only by a ladder, and he used to find with her the fruit of winter in the heat of summer and the fruit of summer in winter. He said: يا مَرْيَمُ أَنَّى لَكِ هذا, she said: هُوَ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ [Āl ʿImrān: 37]. At that, Zakariyyā hoped for a child; he said: the One who brings her this is able to grant me a child. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: most of those made servants of the rabbis became prophets, which is why only boys were accepted. This is the exegesis. The context of the speech is that she said: رَبِّ إِنِّي وَضَعْتُها أُنْثى, i.e. and the female is not among what is accepted, so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: فَتَقَبَّلَها رَبُّها بِقَبُولٍ حَسَنٍ [Āl ʿImrān: 37]. As for the grammar: putting the adjective in the place of the noun it qualifies is not permitted in some places and is permitted figuratively in others, and omitting the lām [i.e. «لك» for a servant] in the like of this is not used.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: قالَتْ رَبِّ إِنِّي وَضَعْتُها أُنْثى: [أنثى is] ḥāl (circumstantial), or, if you wish, a badal (substitute). وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِما وَضَعَتْ: we have mentioned that it is read «بما وضعتُ», and that is a far-fetched reading, because she had already said «إنّي وضعتها أنثى». It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās «بما وضعتِ» with kasra on the tāʾ, i.e. this was said to her. [Translator's note: the source prints both variants with the standard vowelling; the vowels given follow the descriptions.] وَلَيْسَ الذَّكَرُ كَالْأُنْثى: the kāf is in the position of accusative as the khabar (predicate) of ليس, or as an adverb (ẓarf). وَإِنِّي سَمَّيْتُها مَرْيَمَ: two objects; مريم is a diptote because it is a definite feminine name, and it is also foreign. وَذُرِّيَّتَها: conjoined to the hāʾ and alif [i.e. the pronoun ها].

nahhas-irab:37-37.t:
فَتَقَبَّلَها رَبُّها بِقَبُولٍ حَسَنٍ: the maṣdar (verbal noun) of تقبّل is تقبُّل, except that the meaning of تقبّل and قبل is the same, so the meaning is "her Lord received her with a goodly acceptance". Its parallel is [al-Rajaz] 76-
وقد تطوّيت انطواء الحضب
(I coiled myself up as the snake coils.)
because the meaning of تطوّيت and انطويت is the same. Abū Jaʿfar said: الحضب is the snake. Its like is [the verse] of al-Quṭāmī: [al-Wāfir] 77-
وليس بأن تتّبعه اتّباعا
(And it is not by your following it [eagerly] …)
وَأَنْبَتَها نَباتاً حَسَناً: He did not say إنباتا because when He said أنبتها it indicated نبت, as the poet said:
[al-Ṭawīl] 78-
فصرنا إلى الحسنى ورقّ كلامنا ... ورضت فذلّت صعبة أيّ إذلال
(We came round to kindness and our speech grew gentle; I tamed her, and a difficult one became tame, what a taming!)
The maṣdar of ذلّت is only ذُلّ, but it indicated the meaning of أذللت. Mujāhid read «فتقبَّلْها» with sukūn on the lām, as a request and petition, «ربَّها» as an annexed vocative, «وأنبِتْها» with sukūn on the tāʾ, «وكفِّلْها» with sukūn on the lām, «زكرياءَ» with the madd and in the accusative. The Kufans read وَكَفَّلَها زَكَرِيَّا, i.e. "and Allah made Zakariyyā her guardian". Hārūn ibn Mūsā narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Madanī «وكفِلها زكريّاءُ» with kasra on the fāʾ. [Translator's note: the source prints these readings with the standard vowelling; the forms given follow the descriptions.] Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: one says كفَل يكفُل and كفِل يكفَل, and I have not heard كفُل, though it has been mentioned. Al-Farrāʾ said: the people of the Hijaz pronounce زكريّاء with madd and also shorten it, and the people of Najd drop the alif from it and decline it fully, saying زكريٌّ. Al-Akhfash said: there are four dialect forms of it: زكرياء with madd, زكريّا shortened, زكريّ with doubled yāʾ and fully declined, and زكر, «ورأيت زكريا» [Translator's note: the source is garbled at this point; translated as written]. Abū Ḥātim said: زكريّ is not fully declined because it is foreign. This is an error, because anything with a yāʾ like this one is fully declined. زكريّاء is not fully declined, with madd or shortened, because it has a feminine alif; the proof of this is that it is not declined even when indefinite. Some said: it is not declined because it is foreign. كُلَّما دَخَلَ: accusative by وجد, i.e. "every [time of] his entering", i.e. every time he entered. If you wish, you may incline (imāla) the alif of «حساب» because of the kasra of the ḥāʾ.

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: هُنالِكَ: in the position of accusative (manṣūb), because it is an adverb (ẓarf) that includes place and states of time. It is indeclinable (mabnī) because it is on a par with ذلك, and هنا is on a par with هذا. The Banū Tamīm say هناك in the sense of هنالك. The lām has kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. ذُرِّيَّةً طَيِّبَةً: [the adjective is feminine] according to the wording.

nahhas-irab:39-39.t:
فَنادَتْهُ الْمَلائِكَةُ: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās read «فناداه الملائكة», and this is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd. It is narrated via Jarīr, from Mughīra, from Ibrāhīm: ʿAbd Allāh used to make الملائكة masculine throughout the Quran. Abū ʿUbayd said: I choose that in opposition to the polytheists, because they said the angels are daughters of Allah. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is an argument from which nothing results, because the Arabs say «قالت الرجال» and «قال الرجال», and likewise with women. How can an argument be made against them by the Quran? If an argument could be made against them by this, they could argue by His saying وَإِذْ قالَتِ الْمَلائِكَةُ [Āl ʿImrān: 42]. Rather, the argument against them is in His saying, Majestic and Mighty: أَشَهِدُوا خَلْقَهُمْ [al-Zukhruf: 19], i.e. they did not witness their creation, so how do they say they are female? It is thus known that this is conjecture and whim. As for فناداه, it is permitted, treating the plural as masculine, and نادته treats it as a feminine group. وَهُوَ قائِمٌ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). يُصَلِّي: in the position of nominative; or, if you wish, accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun. أَنَّ اللَّهَ: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read «إنّ الله», i.e. the angels said: «إن الله». [Translator's note: the source prints their reading with the standard vowelling; the kasra follows from the explanation.] يُبَشِّرُكَ بِيَحْيى: this is the reading of the people of Medina; Ḥamza read «يَبْشُرُك», and Ḥumayd ibn Qays al-Makkī al-Aʿraj read «يُبْشِرُك» with ḍamma on the yāʾ and sukūn on the bāʾ. [Translator's note: the source prints all three with the standard vowelling; the forms given follow the descriptions and the well-known readings.]
Al-Akhfash said: they are three dialect forms with one meaning. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: one says بشرته, i.e. I informed him of something that made joy appear on his skin (بشرة), and بشّرته for intensity. Abū Isḥāq said: one says بشرته أبشُره and أبشِره. Al-Kisāʾī said: I heard Ghanī say بشرته أبشُره. Al-Akhfash said: one says «بسرته فبشر وابشر» [Translator's note: the source prints «بسرته» with sīn, evidently for «بشرته»], i.e. I gladdened him and he was glad; from it is وَأَبْشِرُوا بِالْجَنَّةِ [Fuṣṣilat: 30]. Al-Farrāʾ said: from this one says only أبشر. It is reported from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd: «بشّرته فأبشر», like «قرّرته فأقرّ» and «فطّرته فأفطر», i.e. he complied with me. بِيَحْيى: a diptote, because it is an imperfect verb used as a name; it has also been said: because it is foreign. The view of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh is that if you pluralise it you say يحيَوْن with fatḥa on the yāʾ in every case; the Kufans said: if it is Arabic you give the yāʾ fatḥa, and if it is foreign you give it ḍamma, because its origin is not known. مُصَدِّقاً: ḥāl. بِكَلِمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ: Jesus ﷺ; it has been said: it was made obligatory on him to follow him. وَسَيِّداً وَحَصُوراً وَنَبِيًّا: conjoined. مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ: Abū Isḥāq said: the righteous one is he who renders to Allah, Majestic and Mighty, what He has made obligatory on him, and to people their rights.
